items.headline: No Palestinian workers in settlements until Monday, and crossings closed on election day
items.summary: The army spokesman said that from Sunday until Monday, Palestinian workers will not be allowed into settlements in Judea, Samaria and the Jordan Valley, except in industrial zones and some approved places. On election day, Tuesday, the political leadership has approved barring all Palestinian workers across Judea and Samaria, including in industrial zones, and closing all land crossings. These steps add to measures Chief of Staff Zamir ordered earlier, including cancelling soldiers' leave from Thursday and sending reinforcements. The army also said that over the weekend the army, Border Police and Shin Bet went into about 40 villages and about 400 sites, arrested about 40 people suspected of links to Hamas or Islamic Jihad, incitement, rioting or stone-throwing, seized weapons and destroyed memorials to attackers. The Palestinian Prisoners' Society, quoted by WAFA, counted about 70 arrests across the West Bank from Friday to Saturday morning.

items.headline: Palestinian reports: car smashed in Sinjil, families leave Khirbet Saruj, iron gates near Jenin
items.summary: Quds News Network says settlers smashed a Palestinian car in Sinjil overnight. It also says families in Khirbet Saruj, west of Jenin, are leaving their homes and animal pens because of threats. WAFA reports that the army put up iron gates at the entrance to Marka and on the Jenin-Nablus road near Arraba. These are Palestinian accounts. Israeli sources had not reported them by Sunday morning.

items.headline: Army operation "Roar of Judah" in western Hebron: about 2,000 residents moved out, 10 arrested
items.summary: The army began an operation called "Roar of Judah" (Sha'agat Yehuda) in Hebron on Friday night, after Friday's Route 35 attack that killed two soldiers. Arutz 7 reports that Duvdevan, Maglan, the Paratroopers, Givati reconnaissance reservists, Border Police and the Judea Brigade are taking part, using Shin Bet intelligence. As of Saturday, about 200 buildings had been searched, no weapons had been found and 10 people had been arrested. The Civil Administration also carried out demolitions at the city's northern entrance. The two attackers, Hamouda and Firas al-Ja'aba, came from Ein Dir Bahha in west Hebron. Ynet says the operation is focused on Deir Bahha and al-Jaldeh, and the army believes about 2,000 residents there belong to the al-Ja'aba clan, which it links to Hamas. According to Channel 14's Hillel Bitton Rosen, Defense Minister Katz said the more than 2,000 people moved out will not return until Hamas's infrastructure there has been dealt with. Abu Ali Express says about 400 families were told to leave with one bag each and that the operation is expected to last several days. The Palestinian figures are similar. WAFA quotes Hebron governor Khaled Dudin saying about 1,500 people (more than 200 families) have been moved out so far and another 2,500 are expected to follow, and that at least 13 people were arrested. According to Ynet, the Hebron mayor said shops, factories and roads were destroyed. Hebron schools are closed Sunday and Monday.

items.headline: Hebron Hills council announces 2 new communities and 6 farms after the attack
items.summary: On Saturday night the Hebron Hills Regional Council announced two new communities and six new farms in response to Friday's attack. It said it had the backing of the Defense Ministry's Settlement Administration, the Defense Ministry and Amana. The council named the communities as Meged (between Negohot and Eshkolot) and Nofei Golot (between Otniel and Afka). It named the farms as Mitzpe Tzur near Telem, close to the attack site; Noy, between Karmei Yehuda and Adora; Lev Amit, between Makeda and Adora; Eshel, near Meged; Lemaan Achai, between Otniel and Shima; and Mitzpe Or, between Carmel and the nature reserve in the Judean Desert. Council official Eliram Azoulay is quoted. The names and locations come from the council's own announcement; no government body or other outlet had confirmed them by Sunday morning. In a related story, Arutz 7 reports that more than 100 farm owners signed a letter backing Finance Minister Smotrich.

items.headline: Teen hurt as dozens from Sinjil throw stones at shepherds; flock poisoned near al-Mughayyir
items.summary: On Saturday, dozens of people from Sinjil threw stones at shepherds from the Tzur Levavi farm and at a security vehicle, according to the Yesha Council Situation Room (JSR) and Elisha Yered. A teenager was hit in the head. Hatzalah Yosh said the injury was light and he was treated at the scene. That afternoon, sheep in the Or Nachman flock near al-Mughayyir were poisoned. Hatzalah Yosh said at least three sheep were affected and one died. JSR called it the 17th poisoning this year and Hatzalah Yosh counted 20, so the totals do not match. Hatzalah Yosh's weekend list, posted by Elchanan Groner, also records three firebombs near the Psagot fence and a stone attack on a Ma'ale HaTamar farm resident near Adam on Friday night, and stone attacks on shepherds near Duma and west of Kafr Malik on Saturday. In the same area, WAFA says settlers grazed sheep among homes and fields in Yabrud and al-Mughayyir on Saturday.

items.headline: Suspected shooting at Shara farm from a car out of Beit Ur al-Tahta
items.summary: JSR reports suspected shots fired at Shara farm in western Binyamin from a car that came from Beit Ur al-Tahta. No one was hurt. Elchanan Groner notes that the attacker who critically wounded Neria Leiter came from the same village. The army had not commented by Sunday morning, and no other outlet had reported the incident.

items.headline: Arrests in Burin after the attack on hikers, including the man filmed with a tree trunk
items.summary: On Saturday the army arrested several people in Burin, including the man seen on video hitting people with a tree trunk during Friday's attack on hikers (reported in the 24 October edition). A memorial to attackers was also torn down. Later, stones were thrown at a bus on the Gilad road. Also reported by Abu Ali Express.

items.headline: Shiloh-area settlers accuse soldiers of burning a youth house; protest at Shiloh Junction
items.summary: Elisha Yered says soldiers under a company commander burned a youth house, with tefillin inside, on the Nahalat HaNavi hill near Esh Kodesh, and that Paratroopers Brigade headquarters (Col. Roi Zweig) was called in. Elchanan Groner posted video of a masked soldier holding a club at a protest at Shiloh Junction. According to Yered, Shiloh Junction was then declared a closed military zone and sponge rounds were fired. MK Limor Son Har-Melech demanded an investigation. All of this comes from settler sources. The army had not responded by Sunday morning.

items.headline: Smotrich on Channel 14: "There is no escape from dismantling the Palestinian Authority through a military campaign and cancelling the Oslo Accords"
items.summary: Three days before the election, Religious Zionism leader Bezalel Smotrich said on Channel 14's "HaPatriotim" on Saturday night that Israel must change its policy and act against the Palestinian Authority by military means as well: "There is no escape from dismantling the Palestinian Authority through a military campaign and from canceling the Oslo Accords," Channel 14 reports. On Thursday, Arutz 7 reported that former chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot, who leads the Yashar party, told a rally in Modi'in that if he joins the next government he will work to abolish the additional minister post in the Defense Ministry that Smotrich holds, bring back administrative detention orders and allow about 60,000 to 70,000 Palestinian workers to enter Israel. He also listed demolition of illegal construction among his steps. Smotrich replied, in his own words, that this would "close the Settlement Directorate we built," return settlers to military rule, "evacuate the farms and communities," and end up with "a Palestinian terror state" (Arutz 7). These are campaign statements by the two politicians. Neither report describes a government plan.

items.headline: Unconfirmed weekend reports: stones and firebombs near Psagot and Duma, and a suspected ramming near Havat Gilad (single-source)
items.summary: Hatzala Yosh, a group that posts incident alerts, reported stone-throwing and firebomb incidents in several places in the past 24 hours, according to Elchanan Groner's summary on X, including near Psagot, near Duma and near Ma'ale HaTamar. Separately, Netanel Frankel (@Israel8251) wrote on X that a vehicle tried to ram Israelis at the Havat Gilad area. No casualties are reported in either account, and no army, police or news report confirming the incidents was found. Both are the posters' own claims and are unconfirmed.

items.headline: Netanyahu: "a very big surprise" is waiting for the PA
items.summary: In a Friday evening interview with Neve Dromi on i24NEWS, Prime Minister Netanyahu said that "a very big surprise is also waiting for the Palestinian Authority" but did not say what it was. "I don't declare, I act and then say what we did," he said. He said the order in Hebron was to enter the neighborhood the attackers came from, move out its residents, go house to house to collect weapons and destroy "all the terror infrastructure," as was done in the refugee camps. He said a wider operation against what remains of terror in Judea and Samaria would follow, on a scale not seen since the Six-Day War. PA officials responded the next day. WAFA reported that Vice President Hussein al-Sheikh called for international pressure, and Ynet reported that Prime Minister Mohammad Mustafa and intelligence chief Majed Faraj made similar calls. Also reported by Al-Quds (Hebrew edition).

items.headline: After the Hebron attack, Smotrich orders demolitions of dozens of unpermitted structures near the site and approves four more farms in the southern Hebron Hills
items.summary: Hours after Friday's attack near Hebron that killed two soldiers, Civil Administration enforcement teams began demolishing structures near the scene that the state says were built illegally. Arutz 7 (English) reports that Minister Bezalel Smotrich, who is in charge of settlement and civil matters in the Defense Ministry, came to the site and ordered the work. His office said dozens of structures would be demolished in coordination with the army and the Civil Administration. Smotrich said the aim was to "establish deterrence and exact a price," that the work would continue until Shabbat, and that he had agreed with the prime minister and defense minister to map the area and other locations in Judea and Samaria to widen the effort. He also announced approval of four more farms in the southern Hebron Hills and said he would work to approve four new Israeli communities. The same account is in a second Arutz 7 report, and Ynetnews carries the headline "Smotrich announces establishment of 4 outposts." The Palestinian news agency WAFA reported separately that on Friday Israeli forces demolished a three-apartment residential building belonging to Riyad Amrish in northern Hebron and sealed the city's entrances. This is the Palestinian account of the same events. On Saturday, Elisha Yered wrote on X that bulldozers worked in Hebron on both Friday and Saturday (his own report, not confirmed by a second source). At the scene, Central Command chief Maj. Gen. Avi Blut said the soldiers' bravery prevented a severe attack on civilians and announced a significant operation with a closure of Hebron and Halhul (Arutz 7, Hebrew). The council's separate announcement of two communities and six farms in the Hebron Hills is in another item in this edition.

items.headline: Hebron attack debrief: two gunmen from Hebron, first operational deployment for the Ari Battalion squad; police say there is no suspicion the AFP photographer knew in advance
items.summary: According to the IDF's preliminary debrief, reported by Walla and the Jerusalem Post, two gunmen from Hebron came to the Judea Junction area with a large amount of ammunition, an M4 rifle and a handgun. They arrived in a vehicle with Israeli plates to a scrapyard nearby and watched the soldiers first. A squad-level outpost of the Ari Battalion had been set up at the junction two months earlier, and this was the soldiers' first operational assignment. They went out to set up a checkpoint to stop attackers from reaching Routes 35 and 60. Early reports counted five wounded, two critically. Arutz 7 later reported that two soldiers were killed, and the army killed both attackers. Judea and Samaria District Police commander Maj. Gen. Moshe Pinchi ordered investigators to focus on the use of a "mashtuba," a vehicle taken off the road, and to step up checks and seizures of such vehicles on the main roads. On the photographer: the Yesha Council's Joint Situation Room (JSR) wrote on Telegram that security officials suspected the AFP photographer who published close-up pictures of the attackers knew in advance, and said he told reporters he was on his way to a protest in Beit Jala. Elchanan Groner wrote on X that the suspicion was being checked. Police told Walla that no such suspicion arises, and the IDF said "the entire incident is under investigation." Ynetnews ran a headline saying the IDF is investigating whether the photographer was informed in advance. The suspicion is unconfirmed and the police statement contradicts it.

items.headline: Police regret the timing of a statement on the Itamar security coordinator case, issued the hour of the Hebron attack; Honenu says he fired in the air after a car tried to run him over
items.summary: On Friday morning, shortly after the Hebron attack, the Judea and Samaria police district and the Shin Bet issued a media statement about a case in which the security coordinator of the Itamar Gideonim ridge was arrested over gunfire near Akraba, Elisha Yered wrote on X. Later in the day police expressed regret over the timing of an earlier statement and said such releases require "sensitivity to what is happening on the ground" (Walla, Jerusalem Post; both do not name the case). Yered, quoting the legal-aid group Honenu, named the suspect as Pinchas (Hasi) Ran, a reservist commando whose brother Capt. Or Yosef Ran fell in the battle of Kfar Aza on 7 October 2023. According to Ran, as relayed by Honenu, he fired into the air after a car without license plates tried to run over him and an officer with him, and senior commanders sent letters of support to the court (Yered's X account). This is the suspect's account via his lawyers, and an indictment has been filed, according to Yered's post. The police statement does not describe the evidence.

items.headline: Two soldiers killed as Hebron gunmen open fire at Route 35 checkpoint
items.summary: Two Hamas-affiliated men from Hebron, both 27, drove up in a car with yellow Israeli plates (JPost says an off-road vehicle no longer licensed for the road) and opened fire at a temporary checkpoint at the Hebron exit near Yehuda Junction on Route 35, at about 7:15 Friday morning. Staff Sgt. Ron Yonatan Roytman, 23, of Ashkelon, a squad commander, and Sgt. Yuval Shai Svilem, 20, of Hod Hasharon, both of the Home Front Command's new Ari Battalion on its first Judea and Samaria deployment, were killed; three soldiers were lightly hurt. After a gunbattle of more than 20 minutes, the battalion's deputy commander, a company commander and a 101st Paratroopers officer flanked and killed the two. They carried an M4, a handgun and a lot of ammunition, and the IDF believes they were heading for a larger attack on civilians on Route 35 or inside Israel. Roytman's funeral is Sunday at 11:00 at the Ashkelon military cemetery. Also reported by INN, Ynetnews, Times of Israel and AP; more detail in Arutz 7.

items.headline: Hebron closed; Netanyahu says the refugee-camp operation model will be applied to the attackers' neighborhood
items.summary: Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir approved a full closure of Hebron and surrounding villages and stepped-up arrests (Arutz 7). At the scene, Netanyahu said Hebron and Halhul are closed, a full closure of Judea and Samaria is being prepared, and the "camps model" will be applied to the neighborhood the gunmen came from: evacuating residents, going house to house, seizing weapons and destroying infrastructure, possibly in other cities too, with faster clearing of illegal building along roads (Arutz 7). Central Command chief Avi Bluth announced a "significant counterterror operation" (Arutz 7). Ben Gvir called at the scene for dismantling the PA and ending shared roads (Arutz 7); Smotrich called for a full campaign to dismantle the PA. The IDF says more than 70 wanted men were arrested in Judea and Samaria last week.

items.headline: Civil Administration razes dozens of illegal structures by the attack site; Smotrich announces four new farms in the south Hebron Hills
items.summary: On Smotrich's direct order, the Civil Administration's enforcement unit demolished dozens of illegal Arab structures next to the attack site before Shabbat. "This is only the beginning… Jewish blood is not cheap," he said. He also announced four new farms in the south Hebron Hills, with residents organizing to move onto them before Shabbat, and said it was agreed with the prime minister and defense minister to map more areas for enforcement. Abu Ali Express places the demolitions in the Farsh al-Hawa area. Also reported by Kikar HaShabbat, Ynet and News1. The exact farm sites were not given.

items.headline: Hikers on ATVs attacked with clubs and stones near Burin on the way to Ein Amsha spring
items.summary: Three hikers riding ATVs to the Ein Amsha spring between Yitzhar and Givat Ronen were attacked with clubs and stones and lightly hurt. A victim told Arutz 7 there were 30 to 40 attackers, Arabs and foreign activists; Elchanan Groner and JSR say dozens came from Burin on off-road vehicles with foreign women activists who filmed, and the ATVs were vandalized. Samaria Council head Yossi Dagan demanded arrests and the deportation of the foreigners. Groner adds that the Shai District commander said the off-road vehicles would be dealt with.

items.headline: About 100 left-wing activists stopped at Hizma on the way to the Mukhmas olive harvest
items.summary: Elisha Yered reports that Binyamin police stopped about 100 far-left activists at the Hizma checkpoint as they headed to Mukhmas, near Sha'ar Binyamin. Elchanan Groner reports the IDF let activists, including Roi Elani, stay in the Shiloh valley. Neither report has been confirmed elsewhere.
items.section_name: Palestinian Authority Forces and the Threat

items.headline: Yered: soldiers say they may not chase smuggler convoys in the Hebron Hills (unconfirmed)
items.summary: Elisha Yered relays a soldier's message that troops in the Hebron Hills are not allowed to fire at or chase smugglers' vehicles, which Elchanan Groner says cross the Judean Desert in convoys weekly; two weeks ago a smuggler rammed an IDF Humvee and was released within a day (second post). There is no IDF response, and the claim is unverified.

items.headline: Southern Syria: IDF closes roads near al-Rafid; artillery on Hamidiyah outskirts
items.summary: North Press reports Israeli forces with three vehicles moved west of Saida al-Hanout in south Quneitra on Friday and closed roads west of the al-Za'rura farm near al-Rafid after entering with a bulldozer. Anadolu reports artillery fire on the outskirts of Hamidiyah and western Zubayda. No IDF comment.

items.headline: Police: AFP photographer at the attack scene is not a suspect
items.summary: Early reports, including from JSR and Elchanan Groner, said AFP photographer Hazem Bader was suspected of knowing about the attack in advance. Police later said he is not a suspect, the IDF told AFP no investigation was underway, and the Foreign Press Association called the reports false (AFP via Al-Monitor, Ynetnews).

items.headline: Itamar security coordinator indicted over shooting at a car in Aqraba
items.summary: Prosecutors indicted Pinchas Shem Tov Ran, the security coordinator of Itamar's Gid'onim ridge, alleging he entered Aqraba with a career soldier, checked IDs without authority and fired at a car, badly wounding an 18-year-old woman. He says a car with no plates sped at them and they had to jump aside. His brother, Maj. Or Yosef Ran, fell at Kfar Aza on 7 October; Honenu represents him. Shai District police apologized for issuing the announcement right after the attack (Elisha Yered).
items.section_name: Palestinian Authority Forces and the Threat

items.headline: Families from the Ramat Gan yeshiva will found "Geva Shomron" on the former Paratroopers training base next to Sa-Nur, the 19th new community in northern Samaria
items.summary: A group of families, graduates of the Ramat Gan hesder yeshiva led by Rabbi Yehoshua Shapira and Rabbi Ben Zion Elgazi, is preparing to move onto the land and found a new community called Geva Shomron, Arutz 7 reports. The site is the former training base of the Paratroopers Brigade, next to Sa-Nur, which was evacuated before the 2005 disengagement. Dozens of families toured the site with Samaria Regional Council head Yossi Dagan. The community is part of the "Reconnection Plan" run by the council, the Amana movement and the Settlement Division, which includes 19 new communities in northern Samaria as part of the council's "a million in Samaria" vision. Dagan said the new communities, together with Noa and a renewed Homesh, "take back the space" and connect northern Samaria to the Jordan Valley. "We received a second chance and we will not miss it," he said. Rabbi Shapira said: "For thousands of years we waited to arrive here." Background: in July the cabinet approved a 19th community in the plan, according to VINnews and Channel 14's English site (both dated 15 July). The Arutz 7 report does not give a date for the move or a permit status, so those are unconfirmed.

items.headline: Netanyahu to Arutz 7: "I prefer to do rather than declare" on sovereignty; says his government advanced 104 new communities and there will be no Palestinian state while he is prime minister
items.summary: In a special interview with Channel 7 (Arutz 7), which also ran in English, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said building in Judea and Samaria is "at a record pace." He said "we recognized, organized or built 104 new communities." Asked whether applying sovereignty is the next step, he said, "Well, it was discussed with the President" (President Trump), without giving a date or a step. He added: "I prefer to do rather than declare, unlike some of my rivals on the right who declare instead of doing." On a Palestinian state he said: "As long as I am prime minister of Israel, there will be no Palestinian state. That is the formula for our destruction," and "we made it impossible." Israel votes on Tuesday, and the interview is aimed in part at voters to his right. The 104 figure is the prime minister's own count. Arutz 7 does not say which communities it includes.

items.headline: Ben Gvir tells the Attorney General he will keep attending Negev demolitions, says more than 19,000 illegal structures were demolished on his watch
items.summary: National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir sent Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara a letter on Thursday saying he will keep taking an active part in enforcement and demolition of illegal structures in the Negev, despite her instruction not to. He called her instruction "illegal and without authority." He wrote that no law bars a minister from supervising, visiting and attending events carried out under his ministry, as his predecessors did, and that his presence does not include operational involvement. He said more than 19,000 illegal structures were demolished in the Negev during his term (his figure, not independently confirmed), and that he will keep leading the governance reform and the return of state land, JDN reports. The report does not include the Attorney General's side. Background: on 12 October the Land Enforcement Authority, with hundreds of police, demolished buildings in the Abu Wadi family's Dahiya compound north of Rahat, near Beit Kama. The Rahat municipality said 80 buildings were demolished and about 400 people, about 250 of them students, were left without housing. Police said it enforced court demolition orders, and the Regavim movement said a court had rejected the residents' land claims (Be'er Sheva 7). For the planning background on Bedouin communities and state land, see the Khamaisi backgrounder.

items.headline: Geva Shomron: families from the Ramat Gan hesder yeshiva will found a new community on the old Paratroopers training base by Sa-Nur, a site emptied in the 2005 disengagement
items.summary: A founding group of graduates of the Ramat Gan hesder yeshiva, led by Rabbi Yehoshua Shapira and Rabbi Ben Zion Algazi, is to move onto the ground and found a new community, Geva Shomron, on the site of the former Paratroopers Brigade training base next to Sa-Nur in northern Samaria (Arutz 7; Olam Katan). Sa-Nur was evacuated in the 2005 disengagement. Dozens of families toured the site with Samaria Council head Yossi Dagan and Rabbi Shapira (Arutz 7). The community is part of the 'Hitchabrut' (connection) plan of the Samaria Council, Amana and the Settlement Division for 19 new communities in northern Samaria, and follows cabinet and government decisions led by Defense Minister Israel Katz and Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich (Arutz 7; Olam Katan). Olam Katan adds that a branch of the yeshiva will be set up at the site. Rabbi Shapira: 'For thousands of years we waited to get here... we have been given a second chance for northern Samaria, and we are not missing it.' Dagan: 'We want to fix the disengagement and the Oslo Accords,' naming Noa and the renewed Homesh as the other new communities that, with Geva Shomron, connect northern Samaria to the Jordan Valley. A move-in date and the number of families committed have not been published. Netanel Frankel (@Israel8251) also reported it on X.
items.source: Arutz 7; Olam Katan; Hadashot 0404; Netanel Frankel (@Israel8251) on X

items.headline: Gun licenses: residents of 11 Samaria communities, among them Homesh, Ganim and Kadim, can now apply for private firearms
items.summary: On Thursday the National Security Ministry added 11 communities in Samaria to the list of places whose residents may apply for a private gun license on the basis of where they live, subject to the usual criteria: Asif, Ganim, Har Bazak, Homesh, Kadim, Shira, Havat Yair (Lehi), Maoz Tzvi (Maoz), Havat Gilad (Nezer Shomron), Sahlav and Eival (Arutz 7; Channel 14; Hadashot 0404). Several are the new communities of northern Samaria. Minister Itamar Ben Gvir: 'We are extending this reform to the new communities we established in Samaria... A gun in the right hands saves lives.' Yossi Dagan called Samaria 'the line of defense of the whole State of Israel' and said many residents are combat veterans and reservists.

items.headline: Neot Harim: Dvir Shnerb, wounded in the 2019 Ein Dani spring attack that killed his sister Rina, is among the first 14 families
items.summary: Seven years after the bombing at the Ein Dani spring, where Rina Shnerb was murdered and her brother Dvir and father Rabbi Eitan Shnerb were wounded, Dvir and his wife, an IDF officer, have moved from south Tel Aviv to the new community of Neot Harim, between Neve Tzuf and Nahliel (Arutz 7). At the founding ceremony Rabbi Shnerb recalled asking Prime Minister Netanyahu, on his shiva visit, to found a new community near where his daughter was killed. Dvir: 'To come back here not from a place of pain, but to build a community, a family and a home, is hard to put into words.' Netanel Frankel (@Israel8251) also reported it. Neot Harim's founding was the lead story on Thursday.

items.headline: JSR's Thursday: stones at shepherds near Kfar Tapuach and Orot farm, and at drivers on Route 458, near Yitzhar, on the Dakota road and by al-Mughayyir
items.summary: The JSR situation room reported on Thursday (JSR's own account): Arabs and far-left Israeli activists armed with clubs threw stones at Jewish shepherds about a kilometer west of Kfar Tapuach's western hill, with no injuries; stones from a passing car hit an Israeli vehicle on Route 458 at the Malachei HaShalom junction, damaging the windshield; an attempted attack on a Jewish shepherd at the Orot farm in Gush Etzion; about 20 Arabs stoned a resident between the Avnei Elad neighborhood and the village of Hajjah; stones at residents on the Dakota road from the direction of Khirbet Safa; 20 Arabs attacked an Israeli vehicle near al-Mughayyir; and stones about 100 meters west of the small Yitzhar junction, damaging a windshield. No injuries were reported in any of them. Netanel Frankel (@Israel8251) repeated the list in his daily summary; none of the incidents was confirmed by the IDF or police by Friday morning. JSR posted no new report on its website, where the latest is from 17 October.
items.source: JSR (Telegram and X); Netanel Frankel (@Israel8251) on X

items.headline: JSR: a video on PA social media shows dozens from Abu Falah stoning Jewish shepherds under cover of the harvest, with foreign journalists alongside
items.summary: JSR says a video circulating on Palestinian social media shows dozens of men from Abu Falah, in Binyamin, throwing stones at Jewish shepherds 'under cover of the olive harvest,' accompanied by foreign journalists and photographers. Abu Falah is where photographer Heidi Levine was assaulted; in Wednesday's hearing the judge said the one video of that assault showed it 'in the middle of a much larger event of massive stone-throwing,' and police told the court the stones were thrown by Palestinians. The desk has not seen the video itself, and its date is not confirmed.

items.headline: Homesh: the IDF says Thursday's shooting was not a terror attack
items.summary: On Thursday evening the IDF received a report of gunfire near Homesh and sent forces to search for gunmen; no one was hurt (Walla; Channel 14). A preliminary inquiry found that an Israeli civilian apparently spotted an armed suspect and heard shots, and fired toward the source; the IDF says it was not a terror attack (Srugim; Maariv). Army Radio reported that the shooting was apparently Palestinian, in a clan feud, with no Israelis involved (via Srugim).

items.headline: Duvdevan drills a day of simultaneous attacks around the new communities of northern Samaria and Ariel
items.summary: Troops of the Duvdevan unit finished a 24-hour drill around the new communities in northern Samaria and in Ariel, practicing several emergencies at once inside communities, along roads and in villages (Arutz 7, with IDF video). A company commander told Arutz 7 the aim was to make sure every soldier and commander can act under pressure when 'we have to deal with several events in parallel,' and that the unit is 'ready for any development.'

items.headline: Southern Syria: Syrian state TV says the IDF blew up an empty house in Hamidiyah and fired toward farmland at Kudna, in Quneitra
items.summary: Anadolu, citing Syria's state broadcaster Alikhbariah, reports that on Thursday Israeli forces demolished an abandoned house in Hamidiyah in northern Quneitra, and that troops at western Tal al-Ahmar fired machine guns toward farmland around Kudna, with no casualties reported. The IDF has not commented, and the reports are unconfirmed. Halutzei HaBashan posted nothing new after Wednesday's Mount Bashan post.

items.headline: Police detain 11 foreign activists who stayed in a closed military zone during a harvest
items.summary: Police arrested 11 foreign activists on Thursday after they took part in a Palestinian olive harvest. Police say they were in a closed military zone and refused to leave despite warnings from IDF soldiers (Haaretz). The location was not given in the part of the report the desk could read.

items.headline: Neot Harim: 14 families found a new community in western Binyamin on the 30th day after Netanel Shakron's murder at the nearby Ein Riya spring
items.summary: On Wednesday, 14 founding families moved onto the new community of Neot Harim in western Binyamin, between Neve Tzuf and Nahliel, at a ceremony attended by ministers and Knesset members (Arutz 7; Israel Hayom). The Binyamin Council says it is the third community founded in Binyamin in six months, the second in a few weeks, and the first new community in decades between Neve Tzuf and Nahliel. It is one of the 13 communities in the council approved by the Security Cabinet. To bring the families in, the council opened an access road of about 3.5 km and laid infrastructure on difficult ground. Two farms, run by Tzvi Bar Yosef and Tzvi Laks, had kept an Israeli presence at the site for years (Arutz 7). Israel Hayom says the community is built on state land near Route 450, and that the council's planning began in July, before the attack. Yishai Merling, head of the Settlement Division, said the site 'transforms the Talmonim bloc and northern Binyamin into one continuous area of Jewish communities.' Council head and Yesha Council chairman Israel Ganz said: 'You tried to murder us and make us leave, and today families are moving here to live in a new community. We are here, we have won.' The day before, the government naming committee chose the name Neot Harim and approved names for three more Binyamin communities that the cabinet decision covers: Armonot (formerly Dia), Aya (formerly the Zibda outpost) and Sela (formerly Mevo'ot Yehoshua) (Hityashvut Achshav). Israel Hayom adds that Neot Harim is expected to be the last community founded under the current government, and that councils have sped up move-ins before the election so that approved communities do not stay on paper. What came before: on Sunday, Sept. 20, Netanel Shakron, 48, a father of six from Alei Zahav, was shot dead at the Ein Riya spring near Neve Tzuf, where he had come with his 16-year-old son to immerse before Yom Kippur. An army tracker wounded the gunman, whom the army identifies as Hamas operative Qadri Samara, 37, of Biddu, and Duvdevan troops arrested him hours later at a Ramallah hospital (Arutz 7). Photos are by Michal Giladi and drone photos by Ofir Steinbaum (per @Israel8251, Netanel Frankel of JNS Hebrew; the photo credits are not confirmed elsewhere).
items.source: Arutz 7 (Israel National News); Israel Hayom; Hityashvut Achshav; Netanel Frankel (@Israel8251) on X

items.headline: Halutzei HaBashan welcomes reports of an IDF post on Mount Bashan (Jabal al-Druze) in southern Syria; the IDF has not confirmed it, and a Druze source denies it
items.summary: On Wednesday morning the Halutzei HaBashan (Bashan Pioneers) movement posted on X that there are 'reports of an IDF post being set up on Mount Bashan, deep in the historic region.' It called this 'a welcome and significant step to strengthen Israel's hold on the Bashan,' and added that long-term security 'also requires civilian settlement.' Mount Bashan, in this usage, is Jabal al-Druze (also called Jabal al-Arab), the Druze-majority mountain in Syria's Sweida province, about 1,800 meters high. The reports the group refers to began with the Syrian site Syria 360 on Oct. 17. Citing an unnamed local source, it said dozens of Israeli military helicopters had carried weapons and advanced equipment to the summit over 72 hours, to prepare a base for intelligence, surveillance and early warning, possibly with radar, and that Israeli soldiers, most of them Israeli Druze, had surveyed the site. i24NEWS in Arabic repeated the report on Oct. 20 and noted that there is no official confirmation or independent evidence. Other accounts placed a planned base on Tal Qulaib in southeastern Sweida. On Oct. 22 Asharq Al-Awsat quoted a Druze source opposed to Sheikh Hikmat al-Hijri, who said residents of al-Kafr, on the slopes of Tal Qulaib, see 'no signs of a base being established.' Syrian journalist Omar al-Hariri called the reports fake, though he said Israeli helicopter flights carrying supplies and aid to Sweida are not new. The IDF has made no statement, and the post is unconfirmed. What came before: the IDF moved into the buffer zone and parts of southern Syria in December 2024, after the Assad regime fell. Israel says it is there to keep Hezbollah, Iranian proxies and jihadist groups away from the Golan, and to protect the Druze; in July 2025 the IDF struck Syrian regime forces in Sweida to stop attacks on the Druze there. Halutzei HaBashan was founded in April 2025 by Prof. Amos Azaria of Ariel University. It calls for Jewish settlement in southern Syria, and its activists have crossed the border many times, with the IDF removing them and condemning the crossings as a danger to soldiers (Ynet).
items.source: Halutzei HaBashan on X; i24NEWS (Arabic), citing Syria 360; Asharq Al-Awsat; Ynet

items.headline: Ra'am asks the High Court to freeze demolitions of illegal Arab and Bedouin homes until a new government is formed; Ben Gvir: 'we demolish 24/6'
items.summary: Mansour Abbas and Ra'am, the political arm of the Islamic Movement's southern branch, have petitioned the High Court to freeze administrative and judicial demolition orders, and evictions from state land, in the Negev and across Arab communities during the election period and until a new government is formed. They also ask that every demolition in that period need the attorney general's approval (Channel 14; al-Qabas). The petition argues that the 'illegality' of many buildings is 'a temporary situation, dependent on government decisions,' and that demolitions now 'decide in advance what the next government may decide otherwise.' Ra'am accuses National Security Minister Ben Gvir of using demolitions for his campaign. According to al-Qabas, the petition follows the demolition of more than 70 homes and a mosque in Dhahiya, north of Rahat, and demolition orders served in az-Zayadna, and the court has asked the attorney general to respond by Tuesday. Ben Gvir told Channel 14 that the Israel Land Authority, the Green Patrol, the enforcement authority and police units 'demolish all year... 24/6. Whoever builds illegally will have his house demolished.' Background: the Khamaisi Plan backgrounder on this site explains the Arab and Bedouin planning program behind such claims.

items.headline: Eastern border: a reservist finds a bag with five rifles smuggled from Jordan; Regavim warns that smugglers have switched to GPS helium balloons after 100 kg of drugs landed at Ein Yahav
items.summary: On Wednesday a reservist from a security outpost on the Jordan border found a suspicious bag in the field during a patrol. Border Police and troops of the Jordan Valley Brigade recovered five weapons: three Kalashnikov rifles and two M4s. They were handed to the central unit of the police Judea and Samaria District, which is checking who tried to smuggle them and whether they were meant for terror or for crime in Arab communities inside Israel (JDN). Elchanan Groner credits the new security outposts along the border. Separately, Israel Hayom and HaKol HaYehudi report that smugglers on the Jordanian and Egyptian borders have begun to use helium balloons with GPS and timed release, which carry no radio link that jamming can stop. On Sunday about 100 kg of drugs landed in the fields of Moshav Ein Yahav in the Arava. Yehuda Kapah, Regavim's southern director, says drug money pays for weapons and calls for more army and police in the Negev, tougher sentences and treating smuggling as a security offense. Israel Hayom cites estimates of more than 100,000 illegal weapons a year in the region; that figure is unconfirmed.
items.source: JDN; Elchanan Groner on X; Israel Hayom; HaKol HaYehudi (Regavim)

items.headline: After the China training report, Smotrich calls for dismantling the PA and a 'preemptive war' in Judea and Samaria; Ben Gvir and MK Sukkot say they warned
items.summary: Responding on Wednesday to HaKol HaYehudi's report that PA officers are trained in China in armor, sniping and anti-tank warfare (on this page yesterday), Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich wrote that there is 'no choice but the complete dismantling of the Palestinian Authority and the cancellation of the Oslo Accords.' He said 'nests of terror of tens of thousands of terrorists' are being built 'under our noses,' called it '7.10 on steroids,' and said that he has not transferred 'a single shekel' to the PA for a year and a half, and that Israel 'will have no choice but to go to a preemptive war in Judea and Samaria.' National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir said he was the only one in the cabinet who opposed propping up the PA and sending it money. MK Zvi Sukkot, who chairs the Knesset subcommittee on Judea and Samaria, called the report 'a serious security warning light' at a time when Israel is preparing for a scenario of 'turned guns' in Judea and Samaria. The IDF, the Shin Bet and COGAT have still not answered the report's substance.
items.section_name: Palestinian Authority Forces and the Threat

items.headline: JSR: the PA's Ramallah governor meets a freed prisoner convicted of attempted murder, then a PA brigadier whose brother is serving 25 years, and praises the 'fighting prisoner'
items.summary: JSR reports that Laila Ghannam, the Palestinian Authority's governor of Ramallah and al-Bireh, posted on Facebook on Wednesday about meeting Saad Jaber of the al-Amari camp. JSR says Jaber was convicted of attempted murder, shooting at people and making explosive or incendiary devices, sentenced to 35 years, and freed in February 2025 in the hostage deal with Hamas. Ghannam congratulated him on his engagement and praised the 'prisoners' still held. Later that day she met Brig. Gen. Ikrima Thabet, a senior officer in the PA security services and a Fatah figure, whose brother Musallama is serving 25 years in Israel. JSR quotes her as calling him 'the fighting prisoner' and writing, 'We are proud of brother Ikrima and this family.' This is JSR's account. The desk did not see the Facebook posts and could not confirm the sentences independently. What came before: JSR's report last week on Ghannam's university deal in Rome (on this page 16 Oct) and its earlier file on her hosting of convicted attackers.
items.section_name: Palestinian Authority Forces and the Threat

items.headline: JSR, Wednesday: a resident hurt by stones near Tzur Binyahu, an attempt to grab a driver's weapon in Samaria, three stonings on Route 60 and on a farm near Geva Binyamin
items.summary: JSR's incident log for Wednesday, as JSR tells it: in the morning, a shepherd from the Nekuda BaEmek farm east of Turmus Ayya was attacked while about 30 Arabs gathered, with no one hurt. About 15 to 20 Arabs stoned a residents' Ranger utility vehicle near Tzur Binyahu, injuring one person and breaking the windshield. Arabs blocked an access path in the grazing land of the Kela David farm in Binyamin with rocks. In the afternoon, in Samaria, attackers stoned an Israeli car and tried and failed to grab the driver's weapon, then stoned the troops who came; there were no injuries. In the evening, stones broke windshields on Route 60 near the Trifi quarries south of Ofra and about 1.5 km south of Rehelim junction, and about 20 Bedouin threw stones at four residents of the Ma'ale HaTamar farm near Geva Binyamin, with no injuries. JSR also reported that Arab Telegram channels in Judea and Samaria were spreading a picture of an armed masked man with the caption 'We will invade your outposts... We will resist until you are annihilated.' A volunteer summary on X (@Israel8251) repeats the log. The desk found no second, independent report of the injury at Tzur Binyahu.

items.headline: Suspected ramming at Ramat Migron: a commercial vehicle hits a man and flees, and is caught at Ofra junction after it crashes into another car
items.summary: Shortly before 5:30 p.m. on Wednesday a commercial vehicle hit a man at Ramat Migron in Binyamin and drove off. The man was lightly hurt (Channel 14; JSR). After a chase the vehicle hit another car at Ofra junction, apparently without injuries, and Judea and Samaria District police and troops arrested the driver and opened an investigation (police statement via Srugim and Kikar HaShabbat). The police called it an 'attempted ramming.' As of this edition no outlet had named the driver or said whether a nationalist motive was established, so the incident should be treated as a suspected attack. What came before: on Monday JSR reported an attempted ramming near Sinjil. In November 2022 a young woman was seriously hurt in a ramming on Route 60 near Migron, and troops shot the driver dead (Mivzak Live).
items.source: Channel 14; JSR (Telegram and X); Israel Police via Srugim and Kikar HaShabbat; Mivzak Live

items.headline: Awarta: the tomb of Elazar the Priest is set on fire and the video spreads on Arab networks with songs glorifying the attackers; the Samaria Council restores it overnight under army guard
items.summary: On Wednesday afternoon the tomb of Elazar son of Aaron in the village of Awarta, south of Nablus, was set on fire. Elchanan Groner posted the video, which he says was shared on Arab networks with songs glorifying the attackers. The IDF said troops went to the area after a report and footage of the arson, searched for the suspects, who had fled, and opened an investigation with Judea and Samaria District police and forensic teams. No one was hurt (JDN; Israel Hayom). Dozens of Jews came to pray afterward. According to JDN and Groner, Border Police ordered them to leave instead of pursuing the arsonists. That night Samaria Council head Yossi Dagan, the council's holy-sites staff and troops of Battalion 8208 whitewashed and repainted the tomb. Dagan said the arsonists 'behave like ISIS' and called for 'a determined military response' (Kol Rega; Channel 14). Palestinian outlets reported troops searching homes in Awarta during the night while Jews prayed at the site, which they call the shrine of al-Uzayr (Quds News Network). What came before: on 11 May 2026 villagers raised a PFLP flag over the nearby tomb of the Seventy Elders and wrote 'October 7, a legendary day' on its walls (JSR). In August 2025 Elazar's tomb was sprayed with graffiti in the name of the PFLP's Abu Ali Mustafa Brigades, and in 2011 its stone was partly smashed (Arutz 7). Awarta is the home village of the men who murdered the Fogel family in Itamar in 2011, as Groner also notes.
items.source: JDN; Israel Hayom; Kol Rega; Channel 14; Elchanan Groner on X; Quds News Network (Telegram); JSR; Arutz 7

items.headline: A day of staged harvests: Deir Jarir is closed, Pollak brings 40 activists for two pickers, and an uncoordinated Rabbis for Human Rights harvest at Nahalin ends with about 80 held, U.S. nominee Brad Lander among them
items.summary: Wednesday was the day the Binyamin Council had warned about. At Deir Jarir, where flyers from left-wing groups and the PA's Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission had called on local Arabs, 'especially the shabab,' to join a 'harvest' toward nearby Jewish communities (Elisha Yered), JSR reports that foreign journalists arrived by prior arrangement with the organizers and that villagers blocked a road with stones to keep troops out. The army closed the area and the event did not take place. In the Shiloh Valley, JSR filmed far-left activist Jonathan Pollak escorting two Palestinian pickers while about 40 activists and journalists stood by. The largest event was near the fence of Beitar Illit, on land of the village of Nahalin. Rabbis for Human Rights organized it, and Groner identifies one leader as the group's Anton Goodman. Troops, Border Police and police held about 80 Israeli and foreign activists. The army says the harvest was not coordinated, that coordination is required for security, and that about 100 coordinated harvests have taken place this season without unusual incidents (Arutz 7). Police released Brad Lander, the Democratic nominee for New York's 10th congressional district, once they learned who he was. By evening most had been released, and four foreigners were held for deportation hearings (Srugim). The other side, briefly: the Times of Israel reports that a Civil Administration map given to Palestinian farmers does not mark the spot as needing coordination. The army answers that the plot was not on the map because its owners had never before asked to harvest there. Lander called the detentions part of 'very clearly state-sponsored ethnic cleansing.'
items.source: JSR (Telegram and X); Arutz 7 (IDF statement); Srugim and Walla (police); Times of Israel; Elisha Yered and Elchanan Groner on X; Abu Ali Express; JTA

items.headline: Olive Leaf: nine of the ten suspects go home; the judge says the one video of the Levine assault shows it in the middle of heavy stone-throwing, and the Belgians have given police only an affidavit
items.summary: At the end of Wednesday's hearings, nine of the ten Israelis arrested on Monday in Operation 'Olive Leaf' were sent to house arrest. One was kept in custody: the judge said the suspicion that he took part in the attack on the European diplomats at Taybeh had grown stronger, and she extended his detention by six days. The case against the second Taybeh suspect had weakened and, in her words, was 'below the minimum threshold' (i24NEWS). So far police have received only an affidavit from the Belgian diplomats. On the four suspects in the assault on photographer Heidi Levine at Abu Falah, the judge found that the reasonable suspicion had not grown stronger. She wrote that 'from the single video shown to me' the assault took place 'in the middle of a much larger event of massive stone-throwing,' and that other journalists ran away because of the stones. The police representative told the court that the stone-throwing was done by Palestinians, so the state does not accuse the suspects of taking part in it. All four deny any link to the attack and do not place themselves at the scene. JTA, citing Haaretz, also reports nine of the ten released. The Times of Israel names the suspect whose detention was extended as Nadav Cohen Tzemach. It says he was arrested in December 2025 on suspicion of running over a Palestinian with an ATV and firing a weapon in a village, and was never charged; the desk has not checked this. Elisha Yered asked on X why the diplomats were 'so afraid' to testify and hand their videos to the police. What came before: on Tuesday this page reported that the defense said the case file showed Levine standing beside masked Arabs with slingshots, and that the French mayor had filed no complaint.
items.source: i24NEWS (Hebrew); JTA; Times of Israel; Elisha Yered on X

items.headline: The PA claims 23 'harvest attacks'; none confirmed by the IDF or police
items.summary: The PA claims 23 'harvest attacks' on Wednesday. Its Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission, quoted by WAFA, counted 23 incidents against farmers and harvesters between 6 a.m. and 6 p.m., ten of them in the Nablus district. Among its claims: a farmer was shot in the hand at Usarin, armed settlers fired at pickers at Birin east of Hebron, settlers attacked pickers near the school in Jalud before troops came and beat the farmers, olives were taken at Beit Furik, and land was set on fire at Burqa. The commission also counts the closures at Deir Jarir and Turmus Ayya and the detentions at Nahalin, among them Brad Lander, as attacks, and says farmers at Deir Abu Da'if east of Jenin were made to leave even though their harvest had been coordinated. None of these claims has been confirmed by the IDF or police, and the commission does not separate violence from closures and arrests.
items.source: WAFA (Hebrew), quoting the PA Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission

items.headline: Jerusalem: a plan for 122 homes in towers of up to 12 stories at the Shepherd Hotel site in Shimon HaTzaddik
items.summary: A plan called 'Beit Ramban' proposes 122 apartments, in buildings of up to 12 stories and 47 meters, on about 5.8 dunams at 16 Mount of Olives Road. This is the Shepherd Hotel compound, also known as the Mufti's house, in the Sheikh Jarrah–Shimon HaTzaddik neighborhood. The plan also includes commerce, education and religious space and an underground parking garage, and it preserves the original 1930s building (mynet Jerusalem, from the plan documents of August 2026). The house was built for Haj Amin al-Husseini, the Mufti who collaborated with Nazi Germany. It was bought in 1985 by a company owned by Irving Moskowitz, and building there caused a clash with the Obama administration in 2009 and 2011. The PA's Jerusalem governorate, quoted by WAFA, calls it a 'settlement plan.' The plan has not been approved; the date of its first hearing could not be confirmed.

items.headline: Palestinian claims on Tuesday: caravans added to an outpost north of Sinjil, 250 olive trees cut near Tammun, Madama closed for a tenth day
items.summary: These are the PA's and WAFA's accounts; no IDF or police response was found. The PA's Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission counts 13 incidents on Tuesday. It says caravans were placed to expand an outpost at Batn al-Hallawa, north of Sinjil; settlers cut about 250 fruit-bearing olive trees at Umm al-Kabish, east of Tammun in the northern Jordan Valley, and trees at Marda, east of Salfit; and the army let only about four families and a few farmers over 45 reach groves near Dotan, by Ya'bad. WAFA also reports, citing the village council head, Rami Nassar, that the army has blocked the four entrances to Madama, south of Nablus and below Yitzhar, with earth mounds for ten days. It says a man with chest pains had to be carried out over the hills. The desk found no army explanation for the closure. In Beita, WAFA says, settlers have cut the electricity to a lawyer's house on Jabal al-Urma for a third day; the outpost on that hill has been the site of repeated clashes.
items.source: WAFA (Hebrew); PA Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission

items.headline: JSR, Tuesday: a car hijacked near Shuqba by four masked men, stones on Route 465 and near Funduq, a suspected arson at Nili
items.summary: JSR's other alerts on Tuesday: an Israeli car was hijacked near the village of Shuqba, northwest of Ramallah, by four masked suspects, one of them apparently armed; no one was hurt. A black object was thrown at an Israeli car just past the Yakir junction in Samaria and hit it, without damage. Stones were thrown at an Israeli car on Route 465 near the turn to the Kela David farm in Binyamin, and in the evening near the village of Funduq in Samaria; no injuries were reported. A fire in an apartment at Nili, in Binyamin, was put out by residents, and arson is suspected. JSR also reports that Qalqilya's main Telegram channel posted a tribute on Monday to Uday al-Tamimi, who shot and killed Sgt. Noa Lazar at the Shuafat checkpoint in October 2022. No second source was found for any of these alerts. JSR's website lists no new report or weekly summary since its 17 October report on the French mayor; the latest weekly report on its English briefings page covers 27 September to 4 October.
items.source: JSR (Telegram and X, Hebrew and English)

items.headline: Zamir orders a new Border Police unit for 'nationalist crime,' a joint headquarters and tougher punishment for soldiers on leave at outposts; the Paratroopers move into the Shilo bloc
items.summary: Ynet reports that Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir held a meeting with the heads of Central Command, the Shin Bet's Jewish-terror division, COGAT and the police Judea and Samaria District on violence by Jews. The decisions: a new Border Police framework devoted only to 'nationalist crime' is to be set up next month, and until then soldiers will take over some Border Police posts and checkpoints to free up policemen; the joint army-police-Shin Bet headquarters, closed earlier for lack of forces, will be revived with two Border Police companies; intelligence on such groups is to be strengthened; and Zamir asked for the results of administrative removal orders and a list of the main people involved, with a view to wider use. He also ordered stricter punishment, up to removal from combat service, for soldiers on leave who take part in activity at illegal outposts. A senior security official told Ynet that the army is 'pouring green when the solution is blue' and asked, 'can you imagine a soldier from Battalion 202 shooting at Jews?' Ynet says the 98th Division headquarters and the Paratroopers Brigade, working among other places in the Shilo valley, have already been added. Elisha Yered reports that the brigade's headquarters, under Col. Roi Zweig, a former Samaria Brigade commander, will be in the Shilo bloc for the coming weeks (the name is not confirmed by a second source). He says the move answers 'harvest provocations' and hopes the commander will act firmly against the anarchists and PA rioters who, he says, start and inflame the incidents. Defense Minister Katz ruled out administrative detention for Jews on Monday, as reported here yesterday.

items.headline: The Route 1 'terror cell' arrest began with a false report: the informant admits he lied, and no weapons were found
items.summary: An update to yesterday's item on arrests over feared attacks. The two men seized by Yamam counterterror police and the Shin Bet on Route 1 near Latrun on Monday evening may have been arrested on the strength of a false report. No weapons were found in their car, and on Tuesday investigators found the man who passed on the original tip, who admitted that he had lied (Channel 12 via Arutz 7; Ynet). Reports that the pair planned to attack Teddy Stadium in Jerusalem were also ruled out. Police had announced a third arrest overnight in a crowded area in central Israel of a suspected accomplice. The Shin Bet says the case stays open until checks are complete, and a security official said that 'in such a sensitive period, we take no risks.' The Kafr Aqab and Ma'ale Levona arrests reported yesterday are not affected.

items.headline: Taybeh: the French mayor has filed no police complaint and has not let forensic teams check his car, Channel 14 reports; defense lawyers say the case file shows he was not hurt
items.summary: Channel 14's settlement reporter Elia Aviv reported on Monday night that Bernard Baudoux, the French Communist mayor who says he was beaten near Taybeh on Saturday, has so far not filed a police complaint or let police forensic investigators examine his car (as relayed by Elisha Yered). Honenu's lawyers Daniel Shimshilashvili and Asaf Gonen, who represent the suspects, told Arutz 7 that the investigation material shown to them in court indicates that he 'was not injured at all' in the incident and filed no complaint. Neither claim has been confirmed by the police, who have not commented. Baudoux himself has said he was hit with an iron bar, kicked and pushed to the ground, and a diplomat who was there told Ynet that he was kicked and hurt; AFP reported that his condition did not appear life-threatening. The lawyers also say the file includes footage of photographer Heidi Levine standing for long minutes beside masked Arabs armed with slingshots and stones at Abu Falah; Arutz 7 notes that these are the defense's claims, not findings of the court. According to Arutz 7, seven of the ten men arrested in Monday's 'Olive Leaf' raids were held for two more days and three were sent to house arrest, and the lawyers planned to appeal. One detainee, Honenu says, is a medic who came to treat the wounded and has messages sent in real time that support his alibi.
items.source: Channel 14 (Elia Aviv) via Elisha Yered on X; Arutz 7 (Honenu); Ynet; Israel Hayom (AFP)

items.headline: Binyamin Council warns of a staged 'harvest' at Deir Jarir on Wednesday; activists Pollak and Mohar help block a security road near Abu Falah
items.summary: The Binyamin Regional Council said on Tuesday that the Deir Jarir village council had invited residents, 'especially the youth,' to an olive harvest on Wednesday at 8:30 a.m., together with international activists and representatives of PA ministries, organized with the PA's Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission. The council calls it a planned provocation and asked the army and police to stop it in advance. It also warned that if headlines later speak of a clash 'in the Taybeh area,' readers should remember that the event was called in Deir Jarir and by whom, and not let the name of the nearby Christian village blur the circumstances. The desk did not see the village invitation itself, which the council published. On Tuesday morning about 15 Israeli far-left activists, photographers and Palestinians gathered on the security roads northeast of Khirbet Abu Falah in the Shilo bloc, and stones and rocks were laid across the road, according to JSR and Elchanan Groner, who filmed it and says the area is a closed military zone. Both name the activists Avishai Mohar and Jonathan Pollak. JSR's account rests on Groner's video, and no army or police statement was found. Pollak, as reported here on 17 October, has four convictions and was indicted in 2023 on charges of assaulting police.
items.source: Binyamin Regional Council via JSR; JSR (Telegram and X); Elchanan Groner and Elisha Yered on X

items.headline: A shepherd is attacked and a flock stolen at Chesed LeAvraham farm; troops and police find the sheep hidden in al-Mazra'a ash-Sharqiya, one batch in a garage
items.summary: On Tuesday morning a shepherd from the Chesed LeAvraham farm near Har Hatzor in Binyamin was attacked and his flock was stolen from the farm's grazing land; no one was hurt (JSR; JDN). Police said officers of the Binyamin station were called after a report that a shepherd had been attacked 'in an area approved for grazing,' and that they had begun collecting evidence and testimony. Tracks led to the nearby village of al-Mazra'a ash-Sharqiya. Elisha Yered posted video of young men in the village burning tires, which he says was meant to hamper the chase, and JSR reported that men used slingshots to hurl stones at volunteers who came to search. By the afternoon, Yered reports, troops of the Binyamin Brigade, including soldiers of Battalion 202, and Binyamin police had found sheep in two hiding places in the village. In one, the owners at first refused to open a covered parking garage; the sheep were inside, the farmer identified them by their markings, and they were returned. It is not clear whether the whole flock was recovered, and no arrests were reported. The Palestinian side tells it differently: WAFA says settlers gathered at the village entrance under army protection and 'provoked' residents near their homes, and the PA's Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission says settlers with soldiers searched homes in nearby Silwad, took sheep from one house and saw two young men arrested. Whether that refers to the same recovery is not known. What came before: two flocks were stolen from Binyamin farms on Sunday night, as reported here yesterday.
items.source: JSR (Telegram and X); Israel Police via Elisha Yered on X; JDN; WAFA (Hebrew); PA Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission

items.headline: PA officers are trained in China in armor command, sniping and anti-tank warfare, HaKol HaYehudi finds; Israeli ministers say they were not told
items.summary: An investigation published on Tuesday by HaKol HaYehudi says officers of the Palestinian Authority's security forces have been sent in growing numbers to military courses in China since 2022, in armor, sniping, anti-tank warfare, advanced navigation, maritime operations and command; some courses last several months. Its main example is a PA officer, Hassan Taha, who wrote on Facebook on 20 July 2026 that he had graduated from a course at a Chinese armor academy in Beijing on commanding companies of armored and mechanized vehicles, with photos beside a Chinese officer and Brig. Gen. Ahmad al-Shami, the PA's military attaché in China. The desk did not see the Facebook post itself. The core of the story is confirmed by Chinese and Palestinian official sources: on 3 September 2026 China's office to the PA said that Maj. Gen. Mahmoud Haroun, head of the PA's Military Training Commission, 'thanked China for long providing military training to the Palestinian side,' and the Palestinian site Shfa reported the same meeting, about cooperation 'in training.' HaKol HaYehudi says the ministers and cabinet members it asked had not been briefed. The Defense Ministry, the Civil Administration and the IDF referred the question to one another; the IDF answered only that it 'acts on its own initiative to thwart threats.' The Shin Bet and the Prime Minister's Office had not replied. What came before: the same outlet reported in May 2024 that PA officers had trained in Pakistan, including in armor and artillery (as recalled by Israel Hayom). The TPS news agency carried the China report in English.
items.source: HaKol HaYehudi; Chinese Office to Palestine; Shfa; TPS via IsraelFM
items.section_name: Palestinian Authority Forces and the Threat

items.headline: Galilee: police seize the Abu Latif crime gang's arms cache above Rama, including an IDF-standard explosive charge
items.summary: In a raid on Monday, Northern District police, Border Police and its National Guard found a weapons cache in open ground above the village of Rama in the Galilee, which police link to the Abu Latif crime organization. It held four pistols and eight rifles, including M16s, Kalashnikovs and a shotgun, demolition bricks, a standard IDF explosive charge, dozens of detonation systems, hundreds of rounds, ceramic body armor, a car with forged plates and more than three kilograms of suspected cocaine. Police value the haul at millions of shekels; the investigation continues (Arutz 7; Channel 13; Makor Rishon).

items.headline: A Soroka hospital doctor who swore allegiance to ISIS after 7 October gets 27 months
items.summary: The Beersheba Magistrate's Court sentenced Dr. Mohammed Azzam, who worked at Soroka Medical Center, to 27 months in prison, 12 months suspended and a 15,000-shekel fine (Ynet). Judge Shosh Shitrit found that he consumed ISIS propaganda from 2014 until his arrest in July 2024, swore allegiance to its leader after 7 October and kept guides to making explosives and poisons on his devices. His details were passed to the Health Ministry, which may revoke his license. Elchanan Groner called the sentence 'ridiculous.' He says prosecutors asked for 24 to 36 months and that the maximum for the offense is five years; the desk did not confirm those figures.

items.headline: PA vice president al-Sheikh prepares for the September 2027 elections; the PA's senior officers' course meets
items.summary: WAFA reports that Hussein al-Sheikh, vice president of the PA, met Rami Hamdallah, head of the Central Elections Commission, on Monday to prepare presidential and parliamentary elections, which Mahmoud Abbas has decreed for 11 September 2027. Al-Sheikh said the vote could be brought forward 'if conditions allow,' Separately, Wattan reports that Maj. Gen. Mahmoud Haroun, head of the PA's Military Training Commission, hosted the businessman Bashar al-Masri for a lecture to the 24th senior officers' course of the PA security forces. Both are the PA's own accounts.
items.section_name: Palestinian Authority Forces and the Threat

items.headline: Palestinian claims on Monday: a man shot at Kafr Qaryut, homes attacked in Turmus Ayya, cars burned east of Salfit
items.summary: These are Palestinian accounts, most of them carried by Haaretz and WAFA; no IDF or police response to them was found. At Kafr Qaryut, a man was shot after settlers entered a horse farm near the village; troops used tear gas, and live fire was then reported. In Turmus Ayya, settlers attacked two homes in the morning; a man was hurt in the head and vehicles were set on fire. That was hours before the stoning of the Regavim tour in the same village. Overnight, settlers tried to set vehicles on fire and sprayed graffiti in Khirbet Safa, north of Hebron, and Palestinian media reported vehicles burned overnight in Beit Ummar (Times of Israel). Pupils were taken out of a school in Jalud as settlers came toward it from the Shilo bloc. At Deir Abu Mash'al, soldiers moved harvesters and activists away while an armed settler under international sanctions talked with them. WAFA says farmers were attacked and two vehicles burned in Wadi al-Sha'er, east of Salfit, and that olives were stolen at al-Mazra'a ash-Sharqiya. It also reports that troops arrested Palestinians after harvest incidents at Masafer Yatta and south of Hebron. The PA Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission counts at least 20 'attacks and violations' by settlers and troops against farmers on Monday.
items.source: Haaretz (Hebrew); WAFA (Hebrew); Times of Israel; PA Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission

items.headline: Bidding on the E1 tender closes; Britain threatens sanctions on anyone who builds there
items.summary: Monday was the deadline for bids in the Israel Land Authority's tender for 1,234 housing units in E1, the Mevaseret Adumim neighborhood planned to link Ma'ale Adumim to Jerusalem. On the attorney general's instruction, the authority will not open the bids before 19 November, after the election (Times of Israel, citing Peace Now). Finance Minister Smotrich has petitioned the High Court over the tender (reported here on 6 October). Peace Now has written to the government asking it to warn bidders of the sanctions risk. British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband marked the deadline by warning businesses and individuals not to bid. He said Britain has new powers to sanction those involved in settlement building and plans legislation to ban settlement goods. He also condemned settler violence (GOV.UK; WAFA).
items.source: GOV.UK (Foreign Office); Times of Israel; WAFA (Hebrew); Peace Now

items.headline: 183 dunams declared state land in Gush Etzion, opening the way to plan hundreds of homes at Bar Kochba and completing Pnei Kedem's regularization
items.summary: On Monday two state-land declarations were announced in Gush Etzion, totaling about 183 dunams (about 45 acres). Sixty-four dunams at Bar Kochba are meant to join up the state land already declared there, so that planning of hundreds of housing units can begin. The cabinet approved Bar Kochba as a new community in June 2024, and 603 dunams were declared there in August 2024. Another 119 dunams will regularize the access road to Pnei Kedem, a community founded 26 years ago, which completes its regularization (Arutz 7; Israel Hayom). Finance Minister Smotrich said: 'Against an Eisenkot-Liberman-Golan government that will evacuate communities and set up a Palestinian state, we build, plant and expand.' Gush Etzion council head Yaron Rosenthal also welcomed the move. Israel Hayom calls it probably the last major settlement step Smotrich will finish before the election. The PA's Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission gives matching figures, 182.81 dunams in all: about 64 dunams on lands it assigns to Battir for Bar Kochba, the project once called Nahal Heletz and Neve Ori, and about 119 dunams on lands of Sa'ir and al-Shuyukh for Pnei Kedem, which it says the cabinet made a separate community on 11 December 2025. It says the orders were signed on 18 October (Wattan).
items.source: Arutz 7; Israel Hayom; PA Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission via Wattan

items.headline: Three arrests in two days over feared attacks: Duvdevan in Kafr Aqab, the Yamam on Route 1 at Latrun, and a farm owner at Ma'ale Levona
items.summary: On Sunday night, guided by the Shin Bet, commandos of the Duvdevan unit arrested two Palestinians in Kafr Aqab, north of Jerusalem. The army says they 'were advancing an imminent terror attack' and building a terror infrastructure (Times of Israel; Srugim). On Monday evening, Yamam counterterror police and Shin Bet officers arrested two suspects on Route 1 near the Latrun interchange who, police say, were involved in planning an attack on Israeli civilians. Their identities have not been released (Ynet; Channel 14). On Monday morning two Palestinians tried to get into the Ram farm near Ma'ale Levona. The farm owner carried out the arrest procedure for a suspect, and both were caught after a chase involving the Ma'ale Levona security coordinator, troops and the Binyamin Council's security staff. They are suspected of terror intent (Channel 14; Binyamin Council via Elchanan Groner). An alert at Evyatar on Monday over a suspect turned out to be a false alarm: the suspect was an Israeli civilian (Walla). Overnight into Tuesday, the Quds News Network reported raids in the Dheisheh camp near Bethlehem, where it says a special unit entered before reinforcements arrived, and in Qalqilya, where it named one man arrested, as well as in Qabatiya, Kafr Dan and Deir al-Ghusun. The IDF had not commented by publication.
items.source: Times of Israel; Srugim; Ynet; Channel 14; Walla; Elchanan Groner on X; Quds News Network (Telegram)

items.headline: JSR: stones on Routes 60 and 90, an ATV rider ambushed near Yitzhar, an attempted ramming at Sinjil and a 'harvest' call to confrontation from Kaddum
items.summary: These are the Yesha Council Situation Room's (JSR) own alerts for Monday, posted on Telegram and X. At 7:45 a.m. stones were thrown at an Israeli car on Route 60 between the Trifi quarries junction and Ofra junction; Makor Rishon, citing the Hatzalah Judea and Samaria rescue service, also reports stones on the road between Ofra and Givat Assaf that morning, and at a shepherd from Givat Or. The owner of the Ma'on farm in the Hebron Hills reported stones thrown at his flock. About ten Arabs and anarchists ambushed a resident riding an ATV off-road from Yitzhar to Givat Ronen and threw stones; someone also tried to run him over with a tractor. Stones thrown on Route 90 near Zubeidat in the Jordan Valley caused damage. About 15 Arabs gathered for what JSR calls an illegal harvest at the Shavo farm in the Hebron Hills, and three of them threw stones. A car tried to run down an Israeli hitchhiking on Route 60 south of the Sinjil South junction. Walla also reported a suspected ramming there; no arrest was reported. JSR also says Arab channels are spreading a threatening video of men from Kaddum going out to the harvest 'to confront' Jewish residents. WAFA reports that troops arrested four Kaddum residents, two of them minors, in the village's northern groves on Monday. Apart from the Sinjil and Route 60 reports, no second source was found for these alerts. JSR's website and English briefings page list no new report or weekly summary since 13 October.
items.source: JSR (Telegram and X, Hebrew and English); Makor Rishon; Walla; WAFA (Hebrew)

items.headline: Two flocks stolen in Binyamin in one night: about 90 head from Nof HaMishkan, half found in Talfit, and 40 from Sela Rimon, found in Deir Jarir
items.summary: An update to yesterday's item on the night search in Deir Jarir. JSR reported on Monday morning that 40 sheep had been stolen overnight from the Sela Rimon farm's flock, found in Deir Jarir and all returned to the farm. That account explains the search: Palestinian outlets had reported Israelis and troops searching homes in the village late on Sunday night. Elisha Yered says the flock was driven first to Taybeh and then smuggled on to Deir Jarir. Haaretz, citing activists, gives a different account: it says a settler grazing near homes on the edge of Taybeh left his flock behind, and that activists told the Binyamin regional defense room where it was, but settlers later claimed it had been stolen. Haaretz also carries a resident's account that settlers, with soldiers present, raided a compound on Taybeh's edge and took 25 sheep. The activists' version does not explain how the sheep came to be found in Deir Jarir, and JSR does not say who drove them there. No army or police statement was found. In the second theft, Makor Rishon reports that at about 11 p.m. Arabs broke into the Nof HaMishkan farm near Shilo and took about 90 sheep. The owner is Avichai Suissa. About half were found in an abandoned compound in Talfit; JSR posted footage of them there.
items.source: JSR (Telegram and X); Makor Rishon; Olam Katan; Elchanan Groner and Elisha Yered on X; Haaretz (Hebrew)

items.headline: Katz rules out administrative detention for Jews; Zamir sends a Paratroopers task-force headquarters to Binyamin and Samaria; outpost clearances doubled
items.summary: Defense Minister Israel Katz said on Monday that he will not bring back administrative detention for Jews in Judea and Samaria. He said 'administrative orders are not the solution, rather strong police enforcement,' and that violence by Jews is wholly the job of the police Judea and Samaria District, while the IDF focuses on Palestinian terror (Ynet; Makor Rishon; Haaretz). Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir put the army on its highest alert ahead of the 27 October election and froze leave from Thursday. This confirms the Arutz 7 report of a leave freeze carried here on 18 October. Zamir also ordered the Paratroopers Brigade headquarters into Central Command, to serve as a task-force headquarters between the Samaria and Binyamin brigades, and added a Border Police company (Times of Israel; Walla). Ynet reports that two reserve Border Police companies arrived on Saturday night, with orders that include doubling the number of outpost clearances, and that about 200 clearances of illegal structures have been carried out this year, including in Areas A and B. Structures at the Shirat Tzion outpost were cleared on Sunday; six people were arrested and then released with an order to stay away, and four more were arrested on Monday. Walla reports that between seven and ten outposts are now cleared each week. A senior security official told Walla that 85 harvest sites had been coordinated in recent days, that the army secured the harvest at 65 of them, and that friction stopped picking at only four. Elchanan Groner reports that three outposts in the Shilo bloc were destroyed on Monday morning, and that the Arabs of Abu Falah published a message of thanks for 'the removal of the outpost.' Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich told the Abu Ali Express channel that 'there is a gang of anarchist rioters on our side too, most of them not from the settlement,' that they threaten 'the whole revolution' he has brought about, and that the law-enforcement system has failed totally. In the same interview he said 'the keys to evacuating Khan al-Ahmar are in Netanyahu's hands.'
items.source: Ynet; Makor Rishon; Times of Israel; Walla; Elchanan Groner on X; Abu Ali Express (Telegram)

items.headline: Operation 'Olive Leaf': ten Israelis held over Abu Falah, Taybeh and a house break-in; their lawyers say no evidence was shown and the attackers in the footage were masked
items.summary: Before dawn on Monday, police of the Judea and Samaria District, with the Shin Bet, Border Police and the army and with air support, raided several sites in Binyamin and arrested ten Israelis. Settler activists told the Times of Israel that the raids hit a farm outpost near Ofra and several outposts near Shilo. Police say that two of the ten are suspected in the attack on the European diplomats at Taybeh and four in the attack at Abu Falah in which photographer Heidi Levine was hurt.
