The other four are suspected of taking over a Palestinian house in Area B and breaking a closed-military-zone order. Police showed slingshots found in the raids. At the Jerusalem Magistrate's Court on Monday evening, Ynet reports, three of the Abu Falah suspects were held until Wednesday; the fourth says he was not at the scene, and that claim is being checked. The two Taybeh suspects were held for three more days; they refused to answer questions. Of the four in the house case, three were released under restrictions and one was held. A settler in his twenties from northern Samaria was arrested separately on Sunday over other violent incidents, and prosecutors have filed notice that an indictment is coming. Defense lawyers, among them Asaf Gonen of Honenu and Daniel Shimshilashvili, called them 'ynet arrests' and 'arrests for show.' They say no evidence was presented and that no one can be identified from the videos because the attackers were masked. Shimshilashvili cited the Prime Minister's Office's own line that serious accusations require evidence. Elchanan Groner posted photos of what he says are unmasked Arabs throwing stones at Burqa and Deir Jarir over the weekend, and asked where the arrest operation against them is. Elisha Yered says stone attacks by Arabs are handled by the local police station, while those by Jews go to the district's special headquarters. Israel Hayom's military correspondent called eight arrests 'a drop in the sea' and reports that the army and police blame each other. Ambassador Mike Huckabee called them 'a very positive development.'
items.source: Ynet; Times of Israel; Israel Hayom; Arutz 7; Walla; Elchanan Groner and Elisha Yered on X

items.headline: Turmus Ayya: Palestinians stone a pro-Israel influencers' tour, and a rock smashes the window beside Knesset candidate Fleur Hassan-Nahoum
items.summary: On Monday morning Palestinians in Turmus Ayya, north of Ramallah in Area B, threw rocks at the cars of a Regavim tour for pro-Israel influencers. Fleur Hassan-Nahoum, No. 5 on Ofer Winter's People of Israel (Amcha Yisrael) list, was in one of the cars. Footage from inside her car, carried by the Times of Israel, shows a stone smashing the window behind her; one passenger said their driver told them to lower their heads. Hassan-Nahoum told JNS the group was in three cars when about seven young men 'aggressively surrounded' them and told them to leave. As they turned back, she said, another six to ten were waiting at the exit with large rocks. Regavim's own video, as described by the Jerusalem Post, shows a man in a car telling the group they cannot enter without someone to accompany them, and youths on bikes following and filming them. Regavim had billed the outing as a 'Real Estate Under Occupation' tour of the village's luxury homes; JNS notes that most residents are thought to be U.S.-Palestinian dual citizens. Who was hurt is not fully clear. JSR says Hassan-Nahoum was hurt in the hand. She herself told JNS that a passenger in her car was lightly hurt and was treated by army medics. The Jerusalem Post names the injured woman as content creator Cindy Seni. Police, escorted by soldiers, opened an investigation; no arrests have been reported. Yesha Council chairman Israel Ganz called it 'a real event that is pointedly ignored.' Elisha Yered posted a clip that he says comes from the village's official channel, celebrating the attack with the words 'Entering Turmus Ayya is not like leaving it, dogs of the hills!' over a song praising Hamas bomb-maker Yahya Ayyash; the desk did not check the channel itself. What came before: Haaretz, citing Palestinian witnesses, reports that settlers attacked two homes in the village earlier that morning, hurting a man in the head and burning vehicles; no Israeli account of that was found. The Times of Israel describes Regavim as a pro-settler group that the EU sanctioned in May.
items.source: Times of Israel; JNS; Jerusalem Post; Arutz 7; Channel 14; JSR; Regavim on X; Haaretz (Hebrew); Elisha Yered and Elchanan Groner on X

items.headline: Netanyahu's new security doctrine counts Jewish settlement throughout the Land of Israel as part of national security
items.summary: Netanyahu presented a ten-point national security doctrine on Sunday, drawn up with the National Security Council, nine days before the election. Its fifth principle, on defense, includes buffer zones where needed; Netanyahu said that 'in Judea and Samaria we shifted to an offensive approach and entered the refugee camps, which had essentially become terror camps.' According to Arutz Sheva's account of the document, its tenth principle, 'National Spirit,' lists 'Jewish settlement throughout the Land of Israel' among the components of national security. It also names terrorism and threats along the borders. Gadi Eisenkot called it 'two hollow pages full of slogans' (Ynet).
items.source: Arutz Sheva (English); Times of Israel; Ynet

items.headline: After the live bomb west of al-Mughayyir, troops put a checkpoint at the village's western entrance; overnight raids in Jenin, al-Fawwar and Anabta
items.summary: On Sunday evening troops set up a checkpoint at the western entrance of al-Mughayyir, northeast of Ramallah. The village council head, Amin Abu Alia, told WAFA that soldiers harassed people passing through and damaged vehicles, and that the entrance had been closed in the morning. That is the village's account. WAFA does not mention that on Saturday night a stone roadblock with a flag rigged to a live explosive device was found at Ga'ava junction, just west of the village (JSR, reported here last night), or the stones thrown from the village at shepherds of the Metzudat David farm. Overnight, the Quds News Network reported raids, house searches and arrests in Jenin, the al-Fawwar camp south of Hebron, Anabta near Tulkarm, Qalqilya, Kafr Qalil and Askar near Nablus, and the Ein al-Sultan camp near Jericho. The IDF had not commented by publication.

items.headline: Palestinian claims on Sunday: olives and tools taken in six villages near Nablus and at Masafer Yatta
items.summary: WAFA, citing PA security sources, says Israelis attacked olive harvesters on Sunday in Bazariya, Beita, Qusra, Qabalan, Burqa and Madama near Nablus, beat farmers and took olives and harvesting tools, and that at Beita they cut a power pole and left a house without electricity; at Masafer Yatta it says farmers of the al-Jabour family were chased off and their olives and tools taken. No names, injuries or IDF responses were given. These are Palestinian claims and were not confirmed. Reuters reported seeing at least ten masked Israelis throw stones at harvesters and activists near Salfit, and Border Police firing tear gas toward the hills. The same day JSR reported Palestinian harvesters stoning four Jewish residents at Tapuah junction (in last night's edition).
items.source: WAFA (Hebrew); Middle East Eye (WAFA roundup); Reuters via Straits Times

items.headline: Huckabee at Susya: 'the heart of Israel'; the same day U.S. officials visit Taybeh
items.summary: At the first 'Judea Conference' at ancient Susya on Sunday evening, Ambassador Mike Huckabee said that 80 percent of the Bible took place in Judea and Samaria, according to Makor Rishon's Haggai Segal and other posts on X. One post quotes him as calling the area 'the heart of Israel.' Another quotes him as saying that the United States marked 250 years this year, but that here was a nation nine times as old. No full text or news report of the speech was found, and it is not known whether he spoke about the weekend's violence. Earlier on Sunday Riley Barnes, the State Department's assistant secretary for democracy, human rights and labor, and Brian Burch, the U.S. ambassador to the Holy See, visited the Latin Convent church in the Christian village of Taybeh (Reuters via Straits Times). Heidi Levine's son told Ynet that Huckabee called his mother and told her he was shocked and would press for long detentions for those responsible; no one has been arrested. The EU's foreign-policy spokesman also condemned the attacks on European diplomats and called for full prosecution (Reuters via Ynet).
items.source: Posts on X (Haggai Segal and others); Reuters via Straits Times; Ynet

items.headline: Otzma Yehudit MK Yitzhak Kroizer is questioned under caution over a clash with police at Mitzpe Yericho
items.summary: MK Yitzhak Kroizer (Otzma Yehudit) was questioned under caution by the Lahav 433 police unit on Sunday on suspicion of assaulting police officers at Mitzpe Yericho about a week ago, at the end of a memorial for fallen soldiers that began as a clash between police and civilians (Walla; Channel 14; Kan). Kroizer says he went over to calm things down and was punched, kicked and pepper-sprayed by detectives in front of his ten-year-old son. He also says he waited almost four hours at the police investigations department last week and was not allowed to file a complaint against the officers. He calls the case political persecution by Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara and senior police investigator Boaz Blatt, nine days before the election. The police case against him has not been made public.

items.headline: Police gather material on Rabbi Dov Lior's harvest ruling and wait for the State Attorney to decide on an incitement probe
items.summary: Police have collected the material on Rabbi Dov Lior's ruling that Jews may harvest olives from groves planted by Arabs, and are waiting for the State Attorney's Office to decide whether to open a criminal investigation for incitement (Ynet; Kipa). The check follows a complaint by the left-wing group Rabbis for Human Rights, filed by its acting director, Anton Goodman, for incitement to racism, incitement to violence and soliciting theft. Channel 13 and Arutz 7 quote law-enforcement officials as saying the ruling could be read as a call to theft, while conceding that it contains no explicit call to violence and that the racism charge is doubtful. An IDF source told Ynet that the letter 'encourages violence, theft, incitement and friction.' The Haredi news site Kore headlined the possible investigation of a senior rabbi over a halachic ruling 'Shame.' Rabbis in Gush Etzion, Tzohar and Rabbi David Bigman have already ruled the other way, as reported here last night.

items.headline: JSR: two Jewish shepherds attacked by Arabs in the grazing land of Neriya's farm in the Jordan Valley
items.summary: On Sunday evening JSR, the Yesha Council's situation room, reported that 'Neriya's farm' in the Jordan Valley said two of its Jewish shepherds had been attacked by Arabs in the farm's grazing areas; JSR knew of no injuries. This is JSR's own account, relayed from the farm, and no second source was found. It is JSR's only new alert since the Sunday reports carried in last night's edition. Apart from its 17 October report on the French mayor, JSR's website lists no new report or weekly summary since 13 October. HaKol HaYehudi published a roundup of the weekend's incidents, matching the JSR and Hatzalah lists already reported here.
items.source: JSR (Telegram and X, Hebrew and English); HaKol HaYehudi

items.headline: Deir Jarir: troops and Israelis search homes at night after a report that a flock was stolen; neither side's version is confirmed
items.summary: From about 10 p.m. on Sunday, Palestinian outlets including the Quds News Network reported that Israelis, with soldiers, entered the al-Midan area of Deir Jarir, northeast of Ramallah, and that troops searched several homes and chased young men. A pro-Palestinian account on X said the search followed claims by settlers that residents of Deir Jarir and Taybeh had stolen sheep, and called those claims false. On the Israeli side, an X user posted at 11:36 p.m. that 'again tonight a flock was stolen from a farm in Binyamin,' with a night photo of sheep being driven along a lane; the photo does not show where or when it was taken. No IDF or police statement was found, and it is not known whether any sheep were found. Both sides agree the search concerned a theft complaint. Before dawn on Saturday, intruders broke through the fence of a farm near Susya, took 15 sheep and fled toward Khirbet Ma'in; five were found (HaKol HaYehudi; Hatzalah log).
items.source: Quds News Network and other Palestinian outlets on X; posts on X; HaKol HaYehudi

items.headline: Wadi a-Rahim: the army says Israeli civilians set the storage container on fire, and it removes a nearby illegal outpost
items.summary: An update to last night's item, which said it was not established who set the fire. On Sunday night the IDF said that troops and police were sent to Wadi a-Rahim, south of Hebron, after a fire was spotted near an illegal outpost, and that it later emerged that 'several Israeli civilians who entered the area of the village' had sprayed graffiti and set fire to a container used as a storage shed (Times of Israel). Police crime-scene investigators were at the scene under army guard, and security forces dismantled the outpost during the day. Ynet reports that no one was arrested. IsraelFM's summary said Israelis were detained, but the army statement it carries does not say so.
items.source: IDF via Times of Israel; Ynet; Walla

items.headline: A PA cabinet minister tours Abu Falah and joins the harvest at Turmus Ayya, two days after the Abu Falah clash
items.summary: WAFA, the PA's own news agency, reports that Sami Hijjawi, the Palestinian Authority's minister of local government, toured Sinjil, Turmus Ayya and Abu Falah north of Ramallah on Sunday. At Turmus Ayya he joined the mayor, council members and volunteers helping farmers harvest olives 'in the areas threatened by settlers'; at Abu Falah he met the village council head, Nazem Shuman; in Sinjil he opened newly paved internal roads paid for partly by his ministry. WAFA quotes him as saying his ministry will keep backing local councils 'so that residents can stay on their land.' This is the PA's own account, and it puts a serving PA minister in person at the harvest flashpoints of the past week. It fits what JSR and the Binyamin Council have said: that PA vehicles were at Abu Falah on Friday, when the council says the PA led the march toward the Israeli hill, and that PA police officers joined the harvest at Salfit on 16 October.
items.section_name: Palestinian Authority Forces and the Threat

items.headline: Police say the European missions have not cooperated; still no arrests at Taybeh or Abu Falah, and the army and police trade blame
items.summary: The Israeli account first. Israel Police say the West Bank District commander, Maj. Gen. Moshe Pinchi, has given both weekend cases to the district's central investigative unit, which is working with the Shin Bet. For the Taybeh case, investigators asked through the Foreign Ministry for detailed statements, footage, access to the diplomatic vehicles and permission to take forensic samples; according to police sources, the missions had not cooperated as of Saturday evening (Israel Hayom; Ynet). No arrests had been announced in either case as of Sunday afternoon (Times of Israel). Yesha Council chairman Israel Ganz demanded arrests of 'stone throwers and organizers of disorder, Israelis, Arabs and foreigners alike,' said 'provocateurs and terrorists' are creating chaos under cover of the harvest, and added that Israelis who use violence 'play into their hands.' Israel Hayom's military correspondent reports that the army and police again blame each other: the army says it cannot put a soldier everywhere and that police have arrested no one, while police say the army is the sovereign in the area. Army sources describe 'organized' groups on both sides, Israeli rioters on one and left-wing activists and anarchists on the other, 'each equipped with a camera and a club.' The army plans to reinforce the harvest areas in the coming days. What the other side says: the EU spokesperson 'strongly condemns' the attacks and expects 'full accountability,' and the French foreign ministry called them 'acts of terrorism' (Times of Israel). At Abu Falah, Heidi Levine had surgery on Saturday, including a skin graft; her daughter told the Times of Israel she was also treated for four broken vertebrae and two broken ribs (Ynet, quoting the same daughter, says one broken rib). These figures come from the family, not the hospital. Levine called the Prime Minister's Office statement 'a lie.'
items.source: Israel Hayom (Yotam Dasha; Lilach Shoval); Ynet (Idan Bloemhof); Times of Israel; Al Jazeera

items.headline: JSR: a live bomb on a flag at Ga'ava junction, a dummy beside a 'Nukhba Battalion' PLO flag near Yabrud, and stones at Tapuah
items.summary: This is the Yesha Council Situation Room's (JSR) own account, posted on Sunday on Telegram and X. A stone roadblock with a flag carrying a live explosive device was found on Saturday night at Ga'ava junction, west of al-Mughayyir; the roadblock was cleared and the device made safe. This answers this morning's open question: the flags that Elisha Yered and the Hatzalah log reported on Saturday evening included at least one real bomb. Overnight, a suspicious object was found beside a PLO flag near Yabrud in Binyamin; the flag bore the Arabic words 'Nukhba Battalion 07.10.26,' using the name of the Hamas force that led the 7 October attack, and sappers found that the object was a dummy (photo by Elchanan Groner). On Sunday, JSR says about 20 Arabs were harvesting olives near Tapuah junction when four Jewish residents arrived and stones were thrown at them; no one was hurt and nothing was damaged. JSR also published its weekend summary for 16 and 17 October, which matches the Hatzalah log reported this morning: stones on Route 446, firebombs at Kochav Yaakov, a shepherd lightly hurt by stones at Ma'ale Ahuvia, an attempt to grab a security coordinator's weapon, two stone attacks on the Metzudat David farm, an attempted ramming of a jogger, stones near Surif and at Karnei Shomron, stones at troops at Jabal Johar and arson near Turmus Ayya. The IDF has not commented on the devices.
items.source: JSR (Telegram and X, Hebrew and English); Elchanan Groner (photo)

items.headline: Security coordinators protest at the Kirya over a colleague held by the Shin Bet
items.summary: Dozens of settlement security coordinators (rabshatzim) drove in a convoy to the Kirya, the defense headquarters in Tel Aviv, on Sunday morning to protest the arrest and the conditions of detention of the security coordinator of Rekhes HaGidonim near Itamar. He is suspected, with a second man who has been released to house arrest, of taking part in violence against Palestinians near Aqraba about a month ago. The Honenu legal aid group says the Shin Bet held him in a cell about two meters by two by two; about 100 coordinators signed a letter to the defense minister saying he is being treated 'like the worst of terrorists' and that 'a red line has been crossed.' Knesset Deputy Speaker Limor Son Har-Melech says she visited him on Friday. These are the protesters' and Honenu's claims; no Shin Bet response was found. Left-wing critics on X asked who was guarding the settlements during the protest.
items.source: Arutz 7; Elisha Yered on X; Elchanan Groner on X (Son Har-Melech video)

items.headline: Strook says the PA and left-wing groups organize provocations; Eliyahu says violence grows where the state does not answer Arab rioters
items.summary: Settlement Minister Orit Strook told a Makor Rishon conference that she opposes the violence by young Jews and that 'it exists, it cannot be denied and it must be dealt with,' but that it does not represent most farm residents. She said that what has grown more sophisticated is 'the campaign around it,' and that cabinet briefings show preparations by the Palestinian Authority, BDS groups, anti-Israel organizations and Israeli left-wing groups to provoke clashes and drag teenagers into them; she said she cannot give details. That is her claim. Heritage Minister Amichai Eliyahu told Kan that violence appears 'where there is no state response to Arab rioters.' Moran T argued throughout the day on X that the 'settler violence' campaign is driven by those who want a Palestinian state in Judea and Samaria, that the EU funds it, and that Arab violence goes uncondemned; those are her claims. Separately, Arutz 7 reports that Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir has ordered a freeze on leave across the army on election day, 27 October, for fear of escalation on one of the fronts; no second outlet was found (unconfirmed).
items.source: Arutz 7 (Strook at the Makor Rishon conference; Zamir order); Kan via X; Moran T on X

items.headline: Rabbi Bigman rules it is forbidden to buy oil made from olives taken from Palestinians, answering Rabbi Lior
items.summary: What came before: on Friday Rabbi Dov Lior, the former chief rabbi of Kiryat Arba, ruled that Jews may harvest olives from Palestinian-owned groves 'to publicly demonstrate our ownership of the land' (Times of Israel; Haaretz). The Tzohar rabbinic group condemned the ruling, saying theft is forbidden whoever the owner is. On Sunday Rabbi David Bigman, president of the Ma'ale Gilboa yeshiva, published a ruling that it is forbidden to buy olive oil made from olives presumed stolen, and that there is 'no permission at all' to buy from an olive press that boasts of buying such olives; he cites the Shulchan Aruch that buying stolen goods 'strengthens the hands of transgressors.' He adds his voice to rabbis in Gush Etzion and Tzohar who have already written against taking the olives. On Sunday WAFA reported settlers taking olives from farmers at Idhna and Umm Safa; those are Palestinian claims and were not confirmed by the IDF.
items.source: Arutz 7; Times of Israel; Haaretz; WAFA via Times of Israel

items.headline: Huckabee comes to the first 'Judea Conference' at ancient Susya, a first for a U.S. ambassador in the Hebron Hills
items.summary: The Hebron Hills Regional Council and the Hebron local council held their first 'Judea Conference' at ancient Susya on Sunday, funded by the Diaspora Affairs Ministry, with Minister Amichai Chikli and local council heads. Ambassador Mike Huckabee was scheduled to meet participants in the ancient synagogue at 5:45 p.m., give the keynote speech at 6:45 p.m. and attend the signing of a 'Judea Declaration' at 7:15 p.m.; Arutz 7 carried the signing live. Council head Eliram Azulai called it 'a historic moment' and the first visit of a U.S. ambassador to the area. What Huckabee said had not been reported when this edition was published. The visit comes a day after he called the beating of Heidi Levine 'a despicable act of terror.'

items.headline: The central section of the new Route 60 between Gush Etzion and Jerusalem opens
items.summary: The central section of the upgraded Route 60 between Gush Etzion and Jerusalem, about two kilometers long, was to open partly to traffic on Sunday night and fully by the end of the week. It joins the northern and southern sections, already open, for a total of about 4.5 kilometers. The Transportation Ministry project, carried out by the Moriah company, is estimated at about 490 million shekels and also includes a sunken Hashayarot junction and an underpass; the Efrat North junction is next.

items.headline: Palestinian claims on Sunday: a trailer set on fire in Wadi Rahim near as-Samu
items.summary: WAFA, the PA news agency, says settlers set fire to a trailer and a tin structure in Wadi Rahim, east of as-Samu south of Hebron, while chasing residents and farmers; Palestinian outlets posted footage of smoke from the trailer and a man using an excavator to put it out (Times of Israel). There were no reports of injuries. These are Palestinian claims; no IDF or police account was found, and who set the fire is not established.

items.headline: About 100 kilograms of hashish fall into the fields of Ein Yahav, apparently from a drone from Jordan
items.summary: On Sunday morning a load of about 100 kilograms of hashish fell into the fields of Moshav Ein Yahav in the Arava, apparently from a cargo drone crossing from Jordan (Srugim; Israel Hayom). No arrests were reported. Regavim called it a warning light of a 'national emergency' on the Jordanian and Egyptian borders, through which it says tens of thousands of weapons have entered; that is Regavim's claim. Separately, on Saturday night shots were heard near a Religious Zionism rally in Lod; police searches found no shooter, scene or injuries (Walla; Israel Hayom). Minister Smotrich said Shin Bet figures he was given show more than a million weapons in Arab society (his claim) and proposed emergency legislation that would treat illegal weapons as terrorism and bring in the Shin Bet.
items.source: Srugim; Israel Hayom; Regavim; Walla; Arutz 7

items.headline: Ramon commandos find a Carlo, two pistols and a Hamas flag in Dura
items.summary: Soldiers of the Ramon reconnaissance unit (6261) stopped a suspicious car in Dura, in the Judah Brigade's sector southwest of Hebron, and found army jackets, a Hamas flag, a fake rifle and stolen Israeli license plates. A search of a nearby garage then turned up an improvised Carlo submachine gun, two pistols, an airsoft pistol, ammunition and military equipment, which were seized. The report comes from the army's account as carried by Arutz 7 and Kipa; the number of people detained was not given.
items.section_name: Palestinian Authority Forces and the Threat

items.headline: Incidents the wire services did not carry: suspected booby-trapped flags near al-Mughayyir and Silwad, stones and an attempted weapon grab
items.summary: On Saturday evening Elisha Yered reported that men from al-Mughayyir had placed flags suspected of being booby-trapped on a road used by Jews west of the village, and that soon afterward men from Silwad placed another flag attached to a suspicious object next to an army post near Route 60. Army sappers were sent. The Hatzalah Judea and Samaria log for the Sabbath also records a stone roadblock with a suspicious object placed by Arabs from al-Mughayyir at 8:20 p.m. Whether the objects were real explosives or dummies has not been reported. On 12 October police said two dummy bombs with PLO flags had been found in Binyamin, and Elchanan Groner has written that several real ones have also been found. The same Hatzalah log lists other incidents. On Friday: harvesters shouted at a jogger on the Silat bypass road near Sanur and then tried to hit him with their car, and a firebomb was thrown at the fence of Kochav Yaakov at 11:30 p.m. On Saturday: stones and an attempted club attack on security men west of Tapuah; an attack on residents south of the place the log calls Bar Kochba, in which one Arab tried to grab a security man's weapon; stones at shepherds of the Metzudat David farm near al-Mughayyir; and stones at residents of Bat Ayin near Surif. The log puts the theft from the farm near Susya at 15 sheep, of which five were found, fewer than the 'dozens' in earlier settler reports. Elchanan Groner also posted a photo that he says shows men from Salem, during a harvest approved by the army and the Civil Administration, photographing buildings in the new settlement of Shalem near Elon Moreh. These are the organizations' and reporters' own accounts and were not confirmed by the IDF or a second outlet.
items.source: Elisha Yered on X; Hatzalah Judea and Samaria log (Elad Huminer on X); Elchanan Groner on X

items.headline: Beit Lid: the shepherd says he was stoned and then hit by a car; the army's first finding was that settlers crashed a stolen car
items.summary: The Saturday incident near Beit Lid, described here last night on the strength of the army's preliminary inquiry, is disputed. Arutz 7 published the account of a Jewish shepherd who says a group of Arabs from Beit Lid threw stones at him. He says he moved away, called his friends and the regional security center, and that the attackers then got into a car and followed him; while he stood a few meters off the path, the car swerved toward him and threw him through the air. Two other residents were hurt, and all three were taken for treatment. Arutz 7 also reports that troops arrested three Arab citizens of Israel from the town of Taibe, in central Israel, on suspicion of involvement, and seized their vehicles. No other outlet has reported these arrests, and the IDF has not confirmed them. The Hatzalah Judea and Samaria log, as posted by its volunteer Elad Huminer, records stones thrown at youths from Shirat Tzion at 11:50 a.m. during the harvest near Beit Lid, a clash in which three people were lightly hurt, one with a head cut treated by Magen David Adom, and a report by the youths that an Arab tried to run them over. Against this, Kan and Ynet reported on Saturday that the army's preliminary inquiry found no ramming, and that Jewish rioters were hurt crashing a Palestinian car they had stolen. Whose car was involved, and whether there was one car or two, has not been explained. The army has not published a final finding.
items.source: Arutz 7; Hatzalah Judea and Samaria log (Elad Huminer on X); Kan; Ynet

items.headline: Abu Falah: a clip from a Hamas-aligned network shows masked village youths slinging stones as they advance on the hill, with press beside them
items.summary: Elisha Yered posted a 52-second clip published by the Quds News Network, which he describes as identified with Hamas, from Friday's clash near Abu Falah, and said it shows clearly how the event began. The desk reviewed the whole clip. It is marked 'Exclusive to Quds Network' and opens with the Arabic caption 'With their bare chests, the youths of Abu Falah confront the settlers.' It is an edited series of at least six shots set to music, not one continuous recording. It shows a group of roughly 20 to 30 people moving up a rocky olive grove toward a large white structure on a hillside. Several masked young men swing and release slings at three points in the clip, and another man throws an object by hand. Four to six people in blue helmets and vests marked PRESS move with the group, and others film on phones. Smoke rises near the white structure in the last shot. No Israelis or soldiers can be identified, and nothing is seen being thrown toward the group; no fireworks appear. This supports the settler account that village youths advanced on the hill slinging stones, with press moving among them. The clip starts in the middle of the event, with a man already swinging a sling, so it does not show who threw first, and it does not show the beating of Heidi Levine.
items.source: Elisha Yered on X; Quds News Network clip (reviewed by the desk)

items.headline: Netanyahu calls Jewish violence a 'plague' but urges caution; Eli Cohen wants far-left activists kept out; Rubio asks Israel to act
items.summary: In an interview with i24NEWS on Saturday night, Prime Minister Netanyahu called violence by Jews in Judea and Samaria a 'plague' and said he had brought in the Shin Bet to 'uproot' it. He also said the cases are being checked, because 'many times we were told things and then it turned out that is not exactly what happened' (Arutz 7). Minister Eli Cohen (Likud) blamed 'extreme left-wing elements' for provocations and said he would ask the head of Central Command to keep them out of the area (Kan). Likud MK Boaz Bismuth said there is no Jewish terror in Judea and Samaria and that he opposes administrative detention orders for Israelis (Kan radio). Kan also quoted an unnamed senior IDF officer as saying that 45 percent of the forces' activity in the area now goes to Jewish nationalist crime; the figure was not explained. From Washington, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the United States is 'very disturbed by those images' and has asked Israel 'to crack down on that stuff' (RTÉ; Kan). Ambassador Mike Huckabee called the beating of Washington Post photographer Heidi Levine a despicable act of terror by masked cowards, and said the attackers should spend years in prison (Arutz 7; Jerusalem Post). Amit Segal, a right-leaning analyst, wrote that Huckabee's words show how much damage the rioters have done to Israel's standing with its best friends.
items.source: Arutz 7 (Netanyahu on i24NEWS); Kan; RTÉ; Jerusalem Post; Amit Segal on X

items.headline: Taybeh: the assault was not filmed, the main witness is an unnamed diplomat, and JSR documents the French mayor's record
items.summary: The case against the attackers at Taybeh still rests mainly on the delegation's own word. Ynet, which interviewed one of the diplomats overnight without naming him, notes that the attack itself was not filmed. What was filmed is Bernard Baudoux, the French mayor, on the ground afterward, and a silver SUV with a broken rear side window. Belgium's foreign ministry spokesman says a window of the consul general's vehicle was broken, while a Guardian photo caption calls the damaged car the mayor's; no Belgian official called it armored (corrected Oct. 18). The diplomat says seven grown men, aged 20 and over, ran at the cars with clubs and iron bars, kicked Baudoux in the head and shouted 'Viva la France' after beating him. He also says the men 'probably' did not come from a nearby farm but from far away and were 'called in especially,' and that the delegation is 'convinced' it was an organized action aimed at Europeans. He gave no evidence for these points. Baudoux told AFP he was kicked and hit with iron bars. The delegation calls the claim that the visit needed coordination 'misleading,' since Taybeh is in Area B. The IDF did not say the diplomats needed a permit. It said the visit was not coordinated, so no troops were there to protect it, and Taybeh has been a closed military zone for non-resident Israelis since 9 August, which applies to the Israeli activists who came with the delegation. Haaretz, citing the army's preliminary inquiry, reports that warnings of settler threats reached the Binyamin Brigade operations room by 1 p.m., and activists sent more at 1:30 p.m. The room did not recognize the number and ignored the reports. Forces heard of the attack only around 3 p.m., when it was over, and the army has set up a special team to examine its handling. Overnight the Yesha Council's Situation Room (JSR) published a report on Baudoux, and its main points hold up against the original sources. On 26 April 2025 he gave one of the official speeches at a pro-Palestinian day in Maubeuge, where a representative of AFPS (France Palestine Solidarity Association) also spoke. More than 11,000 euros were collected there: 1,500 euros went to a group in Grande-Synthe and the rest to the association's regional branch, according to the branch's own website. On 7 October 2023 AFPS called the Hamas attack 'a military operation of the weak against the strong' and warned against using the word 'terrorist,' according to its own statement. JSR itself says this does not show that Baudoux is a member or shares all of the group's views. No arrests had been reported by early Sunday.
items.source: Ynet; AFP; Haaretz; IDF; JSR (Yesha Council Situation Room); AFPS statement of 7 Oct 2023; AFPS Nord-Pas-de-Calais website

items.headline: Taybeh: masked Israelis confront an uncoordinated European delegation in a closed zone; the French mayor on the ground is the pro-Palestinian twin-town mayor
items.summary: The IDF says the European visit to the olive harvest at Taybeh on Saturday afternoon was not coordinated with the army, and that the alert was sent to a brigade operations account meant only for security personnel; by its preliminary inquiry no troops were there at the time. Since 9 August the army has kept Taybeh a closed military zone for non-resident Israelis (Reuters; Straits Times). After the Sabbath, the Prime Minister's Office issued a statement headed 'Serious accusations require serious evidence.' It said the delegation entered a sensitive area 'without prior coordination with the IDF, as officially confirmed by the military'; that the visit included Bernard Baudoux, 'a French Communist Party mayor' who had raised the Palestinian flag over his city hall until French authorities had it removed; that the published images 'do not establish the complete sequence of events or individual responsibility'; and that the reports come amid 'a coordinated campaign to smear Israel' during the harvest. What it says about Baudoux is correct: AFP and L'Humanité, the Communist daily, call him a Communist mayor, and L'Observateur reported in September 2025 that the sub-prefecture had the flag taken down the same afternoon. In May 2018 he also demanded 'strong sanctions' by France against Israel (L'Observateur), as Elisha Yered and Elchanan Groner pointed out. The office's doubt about who attacked goes further than the army and Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar, who both blamed 'Israeli rioters'; Sa'ar added that it was 'unfortunate' the visit was not coordinated (Ynet; Arutz 7). The office offered no evidence of a coordinated campaign. Yesha Council chairman Israel Ganz said that 'provocateurs and terrorists' use the harvest to create clashes and that 'in many cases they are the ones attacking,' but also that 'Israelis who resort to violence play into their hands'; he demanded that police arrest stone throwers and organizers on every side at events known in advance, instead of opening an investigation afterward (JSR). Baudoux told AFP the attack shows Israel's 'tolerance' of settler violence. According to L'Humanité, he had come with a Catholic bishop from Cambrai and the parish priest of Aulnoye-Aymeries for the official signing of the twinning; the Belgian foreign minister also mentions 'catholic representatives.' Israeli activists nonetheless accompanied the delegation: Amit Orfali told Haaretz he came with another activist after Palestinians reported that settlers were taking sacks of olives. The man filmed on the ground was not a consul, as Army Radio and WAFA first said. He is Bernard Baudoux, 78, mayor of Aulnoye-Aymeries in northern France (Haaretz; the Belgian foreign minister speaks only of 'a French mayor'). In July his council voted to twin the town with Taybeh and he announced an autumn delegation; last year he flew the Palestinian flag on his city hall and called West Bank settlement 'a spoliation of Palestinian lands,' while also saying Hamas must free the Israeli hostages (Canal FM; L'Observateur). Moran T called him a known Israel-hater; that overstates it, but she was right that this was a politically organized visit and not a chance encounter. The first reports also did not hold up in other details. Army Radio said a car was pelted with stones; the three clips it published show masked young men with sticks at a car window, ATVs following the cars, and the mayor on the ground, but no stone-throwing, no broken window and no blow. AFP, citing witnesses and diplomats, says the men kicked Baudoux; two people who spoke to him said he did not need hospital care. The kicks are not in the clips examined. Ynet placed the mayor in Olonne-sur-Mer, which is wrong. At least one pro-Palestinian account said American and British diplomats were attacked; the delegations were French, Belgian and Polish. What is established: about seven masked Israelis on ATVs surrounded the cars, demanded IDs and broke a car window; Belgium's foreign ministry spokesman says it was the consul general's vehicle, the minister said only that 'a Belgian vehicle was damaged,' and a Guardian photo caption calls it the mayor's car (Army Radio; Haaretz; WAFA; Belga; corrected Oct. 18). The IDF condemned 'Israeli rioters,' and police opened an investigation and asked the Foreign Ministry to help find the victims. No arrests had been reported by Saturday night. What came before: Taybeh has been a flashpoint since 2025. Last July, international outlets reported that settlers set fire to the ancient St. George church; police found the fire was in open ground nearby and the church was not damaged, and U.S. Ambassador Huckabee, who had called it terror, said he had attributed it to no one (Ynet; Channel 14). JDN, reporting the Binyamin Council's case, says the images used as proof show Jewish herders trying to put the fire out. The fire's cause was never determined. The village priest, Bashar Fawadleh, who sits on the board of Kairos Palestine, is the Taybeh organizer of the twinning with Aulnoye-Aymeries (Canal FM). Residents and church leaders report repeated grazing, arson and harassment by settlers from nearby outposts (Times of Israel; OSV News). Whether the spot of Saturday's confrontation lies inside the closed zone, and in Area B or C, is not confirmed.
items.source: IDF spokesperson; Israel Police; Army Radio (Doron Kadosh); Haaretz (Rozovsky and Golan); Belgian Foreign Minister; Reuters via Straits Times; Canal FM; L'Observateur; Ynet; Channel 14; JDN; WAFA; Prime Minister's Office (after the Sabbath); Foreign Minister Sa'ar via Ynet and Arutz 7; Israel Ganz via JSR; AFP via BFM TV; L'Humanité; Elisha Yered and Elchanan Groner on X

items.headline: Ma'in: settlers say their flock was stolen first, and the army says both sides took sheep; near Beit Lid, a reported ramming turns out to be a stolen car
items.summary: In Ma'in in the South Hebron Hills, settlers say Palestinians stole a flock from them near Ma'on, and that they went to the village to get it back; stones were thrown and troops fired in the air to break it up (Ynet). After the Sabbath, Elisha Yered gave the settlers' account in detail: at about 5 a.m. Arabs broke into a farm near Susya and took dozens of sheep; the trail led to Khirbet Ma'on (the Hebrew name for the hamlet), and part of the flock was found there after hours of searches by farmers, volunteers, soldiers and police. He posted a night security-camera clip, filmed off a screen, of sheep in a lit lane; no face can be seen, and the place cannot be confirmed from it. The IDF said the confrontation began 'amid reports of livestock belonging to Israeli civilians being stolen,' and a military official told the Times of Israel the army knows of livestock theft 'by both sides.' The same official said armed Israelis on ATVs also took Palestinian sheep, which will be returned, and that their identities are unknown. Army Radio's Doron Kadosh posted a daytime security-camera clip of that raid. He says it shows masked Israelis taking the Palestinians' sheep while soldiers pass them without stopping them, and the soldiers then firing in the air to keep Palestinians back; he says the army confirmed the sheep were Palestinian. The clip does show a flock driven down a village street, armed men in uniform arriving and men running, but at its resolution faces cannot be made out. If both accounts are accurate, the theft from the farm in the night came first and the armed raid in the morning followed it. The Palestinian figures do not agree with each other: the Red Crescent says six people were hurt, WAFA says three were hurt and 380 sheep taken. Neither count has been checked independently. Elsewhere on Saturday the reports are thin and come mostly from Palestinian or activist sources. At Deir Jarir, Haaretz published photographs of masked men throwing stones at harvesters, with soldiers near them; when the soldiers arrived is not clear. The Israeli side reports the reverse. Elisha Yered, Elchanan Groner, Amit Segal and Srugim say Palestinian harvesters from Deir Jarir, with left-wing activists filming beside them, threw stones at a shepherd from the Ma'ale Ahuvia farm and then at the soldiers he called. Their clips show masked young men slinging and throwing stones in an olive grove, and a man swinging a sling a few meters from a group holding cameras; Yered says a stone hits the shepherd. The clips carry captions but no time stamps, and they do not show how the clash began. Whether Haaretz and Yered describe the same clash from opposite sides is not established, and the IDF has not commented. What came before: Ma'ale Ahuvia was set up in memory of Ahuvia Sandak, who died in a police chase in 2020, and the state cleared it in April 2021 and again in February 2022 (Honenu; Jerusalem Post); it is now described as a farm. Near Beit Lid in Samaria, the IDF first reported an Israeli civilian hurt after 'a confrontation between several Israeli civilians and several Palestinians,' and early reports spoke of a ramming attack. The army's preliminary inquiry found there was no ramming: Jewish rioters had stolen a Palestinian car, and one of them was hurt in a crash while driving it (Kan). Ynet adds that the settlers had come to stop the harvest and that several Palestinians were hurt by stones; Army Radio, as cited by Anadolu, said they came from the Shirat Tzion outpost. Some right-wing summaries after the Sabbath still repeated only the first IDF statement. Olive theft was reported at Burqa and Umm Safa. At Jalud, the American Substack reporter Jasper Nathaniel says soldiers watched an attack and tear-gassed him; that is his account alone. Yesh Din counts 487 incidents since 27 September, 234 tied to the harvest; that is its own tally. On the Israeli side, JSR on Friday reported stones thrown near Tzon Aviezer, twelve Arabs attacking two hikers near Shilo and stones thrown at a Ma'ale Ahuvia shepherd, and Elisha Yered reported two arrests near Karnei Shomron. None of these reached the wire services.
items.source: Ynet (Idan Blumhof); Times of Israel (Emanuel Fabian); IDF spokesperson; Red Crescent; WAFA; Haaretz; JSR; Elisha Yered; Yesh Din; Elisha Yered, Elchanan Groner and Amit Segal on X; Srugim; Army Radio (Doron Kadosh); Kan; Honenu; Jerusalem Post; Anadolu

items.headline: Abu Falah: the village's history with the outpost, the activists on the ground, and what the inquiry still has to settle
items.summary: The Binyamin Council says the Palestinian Authority brought hundreds of activists and rioters to the hill under cover of the harvest to drag its residents into a clash, and the Prime Minister's Office says about 200 Arabs and far-left activists faced about 40 Israeli youths. The record gives that account some support. Among those on the ground was Jonathan Pollak, a veteran Israeli anti-occupation activist who has been convicted four times and was indicted in 2023 on charges of assaulting police and throwing stones at a Border Police jeep at a Beita protest (+972; Haaretz); the outcome of that case was not found. Jasper Nathaniel, the main witness quoted abroad, is a Substack writer who began reporting in the West Bank in 2024. He told the Columbia Journalism Review in January that he feels 'unshackled, unburdened, by some of the ethics,' that he is 'compromised,' and that he advises his sources; to those who call him an activist, he said, 'I don't care.' His video of a settler clubbing a woman at Turmus Ayya last year did lead to an indictment, so his footage is not to be dismissed, but his commentary is advocacy. The one Palestinian shot, council member Abduljaber Hassan, was hit by soldiers, not settlers; the IDF says he ran at troops with a sharp object. What came before: the hill is contested. On 8 March, Israelis who went up to found a new hill in Area B near the village clashed with villagers, with stones thrown both ways (Srugim; Ynet, which names the nearby outpost as Or Nachman). The army's first call was about Israelis attacking Palestinians near homes; two villagers were shot dead by gunfire whose source was never established, and a third died after inhaling gas. A criminal investigation was opened, and no charges have been reported. Kan has also reported a clash near the village in which, by the settlers' account, a Jewish shepherd was beaten with clubs and stones by dozens of Palestinians and his flock went missing; troops found him bleeding. Palestinians said settlers entered the village and burned a car. On 6 October Elisha Yered and Elchanan Groner reported that villagers spread poison on Israeli pastures (their account). The injuries are not in dispute: Levine's daughter told AP that she has a broken rib, several broken vertebrae and a finger cut to the bone, and she had surgery on Saturday at Beilinson Hospital, which describes her condition as moderate, with injuries to the limbs (Ynet). After the Sabbath, President Isaac Herzog phoned her and apologized; he called the attackers 'criminals' and urged that they be found and prosecuted (his post on X; Times of Israel). Her children told Kan they want a real investigation and arrests. A letter of apology was also sent in the name of Commanders for Israel's Security, a group of about 600 former officials that calls for a basic change in government policy, and a forum of about 200 former police officers; Moshe Ya'alon and Tamir Pardo are among the signers (i24NEWS). Posts that speak of '800 senior officials' count the groups' members; how many signed in person is not clear. Still open: who threw the first stone, whether fireworks were used, who beat Levine, and where her cameras are. The Prime Minister's Office has not released the footage it cited. No arrests had been reported by Saturday night.
items.source: Binyamin Regional Council; Prime Minister's Office; IDF; +972 Magazine; Haaretz; Columbia Journalism Review; Srugim; Ynet; Kan; Elisha Yered and Elchanan Groner on X; AP via Times of Israel; Beilinson Hospital via Ynet; President Herzog; Kan; i24NEWS

items.headline: Claims on each side: where the Israeli sources were right, and what the Palestinian side asserts
items.summary: Israeli sources' claims. Moran T and JSR said the Taybeh and Abu Falah stories were driven by activists and staged for the cameras. Activists were in fact present at both: Israeli activists accompanied the Taybeh delegation into a zone closed to Israelis, and convicted activist Jonathan Pollak was at Abu Falah. Moran T was also right that the last big Taybeh story, that settlers burned the ancient church in 2025, did not hold up: police found the church undamaged, though the cause of the nearby fire was never settled. Her suggestion that the Shin Bet staged Saturday's footage, and her claim that the Taybeh priest was filmed throwing stones, are not supported by anything found. JSR, silent over the Sabbath, had said the Abu Falah harvesters came with fireworks and stones; stones are in the footage, fireworks are not. After the Sabbath, the Prime Minister's Office spoke of 'a coordinated campaign to smear Israel' around the harvest and warned of 'further allegations in the coming days'; it gave no evidence of coordination, though the activist presence at Taybeh and Abu Falah is established. Elisha Yered and Elchanan Groner said Baudoux 'led the provocation' with dozens of anarchists. He came for a twinning ceremony with clergy and diplomats, and reports name only two Israeli activists with the delegation; their point that he once demanded sanctions on Israel (in 2018) is correct. Moran T again suggested that the Shin Bet or the left was behind the footage and compared the story to the Muhammad al-Durrah affair; nothing found supports that. The Palestinian side's claims. WAFA calls the attackers 'colonists' and reported a consul knocked down; it was the French mayor. One account said American and British diplomats were attacked; others said a child and an elderly woman were hurt at Taybeh; none of that is confirmed. The Red Crescent's and WAFA's casualty counts at Ma'in disagree with each other. Press TV's Hebrew account called Baudoux 'a French diplomat'; he is a mayor. An X account quoted Levine's daughter as saying about fifteen masked men attacked her with clubs and nails; that is not in her interview with AP or in any news report checked.
items.source: Moran T on X; JSR; WAFA; Red Crescent; posts on X; Prime Minister's Office; Elisha Yered and Elchanan Groner on X; Press TV (Hebrew)

items.headline: Nachala sets up 'Pioneers of Gaza' beside the border fence and demands that it be moved into the Strip
items.summary: Overnight Thursday the Nachala settlement movement set up an encampment it calls Halutzei Aza (Pioneers of Gaza) in the Simhoni Forest near Kfar Aza, facing the Gaza border fence, with portable homes and temporary structures. Nachala says more than 700 people took part, including bereaved families, wounded soldiers, rabbis and Knesset members. The site is inside Israel, not in the Strip. Nachala calls it temporary and demands that the government order it moved to the 'northern perimeter,' which the Times of Israel describes as the northern section of the settlement bloc Israel evacuated in 2005. Communications Minister Shlomo Karhi (Likud) joined the activists and spoke in support, and MKs Ohad Tal (Religious Zionism) and Limor Son Har-Melech (Otzma Yehudit) backed it on X. Police said they were watching the site in case the settlers tried to cross the fence. Netanyahu has denied that Israel seeks to resettle Gaza (Times of Israel).
items.source: Times of Israel; Nachala on X; Natanel Frankel (@Israel8251) on X

items.headline: Abu Falah: the settlers' account, the footage, and what the evidence settles
items.summary: The Binyamin Council's account is that the Palestinian Authority led hundreds of rioters and activists, with foreign press in tow, toward an Israeli hill under cover of the harvest, and that they threw stones and fireworks; the Prime Minister's Office speaks of about 200 Arabs and far-left activists against about 40 Israeli youths. Village youths did throw stones with slings, and the one Palestinian shot was hit by soldiers, not settlers; the IDF says he ran at troops with a sharp object, which the village denies. Who threw first, and whether fireworks were used, is not settled. The footage, examined frame by frame, also shows the other side of it. Several dozen masked men came down from a new outpost in Area B, set fires and slung stones, and the IDF itself, as quoted by N12, said rioters came down from an illegal outpost. Heidi Levine, 64, a Washington Post photographer in a PRESS vest, was knocked down and struck by four to six hooded men; her cameras, phone and passport were taken. The council's clip saying an Israeli teenager helped her up is edited and does not support that caption. No arrests. Full timeline, background and footage review in the backgrounder.
items.source: Washington Post; CNN; AP; Reuters; N12; Israel Hayom; Arutz 7; JSR; X footage

items.headline: Palestinian and Israeli outlets report vehicles burned and Palestinians injured across the West Bank on Friday
items.summary: Haaretz reported eleven people wounded, including the U.S. photographer, in attacks by settlers on olive harvesters across the West Bank on 16 October, and AP reported that settlers set cars and trees on fire in several villages. WAFA, the official PA news agency, reported three vehicles set on fire near Turmus Ayya. Elchanan Groner cited Palestinian Authority reports that pickup trucks of PA personnel that approached the Shilo bloc during the harvest were set on fire by Jewish civilians, after clashes in which, he wrote, hundreds of Arabs threw stones and fireworks at Jewish residents, who threw stones back. The Palestinian Information Center reported that settlers shot and wounded a Palestinian in Beit Ummar; that report is unconfirmed.

items.headline: Stone attacks on Israelis around the harvest in Samaria and Binyamin; two arrested near Karnei Shomron
items.summary: JSR recorded several incidents on 16 October: stones thrown near Tzon Aviezer in Samaria with no injuries; twelve Arabs attacking two Israeli hikers near Shilo, with no injuries; and stones thrown at a shepherd from the Ma'ale Ahuvia farm in Binyamin. Elchanan Groner reported stones thrown by harvesters at a Jewish car on the slopes of Yitzhar toward Nahal Kana, and posted video of dozens of masked men with clubs leaving the village of Burqa in Binyamin in the morning. Elisha Yered reported that rioters who came under cover of the harvest threw stones at residents near the Avnei Elad neighborhood of Karnei Shomron, and that soldiers arrested two of them. These alerts come from JSR and the named X accounts and were not confirmed by a second source.

items.headline: JSR: Palestinian Authority police officers take part in the olive harvest in Salfit
items.summary: The Judea and Samaria Situation Room (JSR) reported on 16 October that officers of the Palestinian Authority police took part in the olive harvest in the town of Salfit in Samaria, and that the PA police published photos of their participation on its official Facebook page. JSR says the PA has planted tens of thousands of olive trees on state land in Area C over the years, and that dozens of stone-throwing attacks have come from harvest areas since the season began. This is JSR's account; the Facebook post was not checked independently. It follows a Hakol Hayehudi report on 9 October that the PA sends security men in civilian clothes to the harvest.
items.section_name: Palestinian Authority Forces and the Threat

items.headline: IDF and police open an investigation into Abu Falah; Netanyahu's office says it is not clear who began the violence
items.summary: The IDF said troops and Border Police dispersed a violent confrontation near Abu Falah with riot-control means and that a media worker was injured. It said that at another point soldiers fired in the air and then at a suspect who ran at them with a sharp object. According to N12, it also said that dozens of Jewish rioters came down from an illegal outpost. Lt. Col. Ariella Mazor told the Washington Post that troops did not see the assault on Levine and that the soldiers' conduct is under review. Police opened an investigation, and crime-scene investigators were to enter the area under army escort. In a statement in English on X, the Prime Minister's Office condemned violence against anyone. It cited reports that about 200 Arabs and far-left activists confronted about 40 Israeli youths, and it said the inquiry must establish who began the violence. No arrests had been announced by Saturday morning.
items.source: IDF spokesperson via N12 and Times of Israel; Washington Post; Ynet; JTA

items.headline: Triangle: Regavim finds that farmland west of Taybeh beside Moshav Azriel and Route 6 has become 17 illegal villa compounds, with gunfire reaching the moshav
items.summary: Regavim reports that farmland on the western edge of Taybeh, a few meters from the fence of Moshav Azriel and beside Route 6, has become a residential compound of 17 illegal plots, some with large villas, lawns and swimming pools. In 2016 it warned about one building there that far exceeded a permit for a 25-square-meter farm structure. The city of Taybeh replied then that enforcement had begun and the building would be demolished, and the mayor promised in writing to act. That building is now a villa with a pool. The city's representative, Walid Tibi, now says the building dates from 2016 and has been handled by district enforcement inspectors. Regavim says the area has also become a center of constant gunfire, and that bullets have reached homes and yards in Azriel. Its northern director, Neria Shapira, says there is 'a direct link between the loss of governance and control on the ground and violence and terror.' Regavim renewed the warning on X on Wednesday. The report appeared in Olam Katan on 15 October; the account of bullets reaching homes comes from Regavim and residents and has not been confirmed by police.

items.headline: Duvdevan commandos arrest a key weapons dealer of the old Jenin terror network
items.summary: On the morning of 15 October soldiers of the Duvdevan commando unit, guided by the Shin Bet, arrested in Jenin a man whom the IDF described as a key weapons dealer for the Jenin terror network that was dismantled in Operation Iron Wall. According to the IDF, he bought weapons and passed them to the network. His name was not released. The arrest was reported by the Times of Israel, Ynet and Arutz 7 from the IDF statement.

items.headline: JSR: twelve Arabs throw stones at settlers between Burqa and Tzur Harel
items.summary: On 15 October JSR reported that twelve Arabs threw stones at eight Jewish residents between Burqa and Tzur Harel in Binyamin. The same JSR feed also recorded stones thrown at residents extinguishing a fire on the edge of Turmus Ayya on the evening of 14 October, with no injuries or damage reported. Both alerts are JSR's own account and were not matched to a second outlet before this edition.

items.headline: Elisha Yered: the olive harvest as PA agricultural land seizure
items.summary: In Olam Katan on 15 October Elisha Yered wrote that the Arab olive harvest has become a front in the struggle over land in Judea and Samaria, through strategic planting, organized violence and foreign activists. He named PA-linked planting bodies, among them APN (sometimes called the Palestinian JNF), which he said has planted more than two and a half million trees in the last decade near Jewish communities and roads, and he pointed to the PA's anti-settlement committee, led by minister Muayyad Shaaban, as directing harvest riots. The tree figures and committee descriptions are from his column and have not been checked here against PA or Civil Administration data.
items.section_name: Palestinian Authority Forces and the Threat

items.headline: Hatzalah Judea and Samaria: 63 attacks in the first 13 days of October
items.summary: Hatzalah Judea and Samaria Without Borders counted 63 reported Palestinian terror incidents from 1 to 13 October, more than twice the 29 it recorded in all of September, according to a TPS report carried on 15 October. The pace rose during the month: 27 incidents in 1–7 October and 36 in 8–13 October, including rock-throwing, assaults on shepherds, attempted ramming and stabbing, firebombs, arson and suspected poisoning of livestock. Olam Katan separately said attacks had jumped about fourfold in the last two weeks relative to the prior daily rate; both counts are the organizations' own incident lists, not an official IDF tally.
items.source: TPS / Hatzalah Judea and Samaria; Olam Katan

items.headline: JSR: PA Ramallah governor Laila Ghannam signs a university deal in Rome
items.summary: JSR reports that Laila Ghannam, the Palestinian Authority governor of Ramallah and al-Bireh, flew to Rome to sign a cooperation agreement between Sapienza University, Al-Quds University in Ramallah and Bethlehem University. JSR describes her as a public supporter of terrorism who regularly meets released terrorists; it cites as an example her visit last June to Amir Abu Radaha, a former Tanzim activist, after the birth of his son. The university signing is reported on her Facebook page as quoted by JSR; the characterizations of her meetings are JSR's own account.
items.section_name: Palestinian Authority Forces and the Threat

items.headline: JSR: Hamas-style terror cartoon shown to children in a Ramallah mall
items.summary: According to the Judea and Samaria Situation Room (JSR), a video from recent days shows young children in a Ramallah mall watching an animated film on a large screen in which a masked Arab in a keffiyeh throws a firebomb into an IDF tank and flees, and is presented as a hero. JSR says the animation closely resembles footage released by Hamas's Izz ad-Din al-Qassam Brigades of a terrorist climbing an IDF armored carrier and throwing a grenade inside; seven IDF soldiers were killed in that attack on 24 June 2025. The report is JSR's own account; the cartoon itself has not been independently verified here.
items.section_name: Palestinian Authority Forces and the Threat

items.headline: Ateret: a Palestinian driver hits a Jewish youth; the IDF says it was not a terror attack
items.summary: On the evening of 15 October the Judea and Samaria Situation Room (JSR) of the Yesha Council first reported a suspected car-ramming at Ateret Junction in Binyamin, with one person injured and conscious. The IDF and police later said that after an initial inquiry the strike was not a terror attack: youths from a nearby outpost had tried to block Palestinian cars, and a Palestinian driver hit one of them while fleeing; the youth was lightly injured and the driver later turned himself in. Arutz 7 and Ynet reported the same sequence; Judea and Samaria District police opened an investigation into the circumstances.

items.headline: Yesha Council opens a situation room to record friction incidents in real time
items.summary: A new situation room will document clashes between Israelis and Arabs in Judea and Samaria as they happen during the olive harvest, and issue reports in Hebrew and English, according to i24NEWS and to journalist Netanel Frankel (@Israel8251). Its stated aim is to publicize Arab attacks on Jews while not hiding incidents in the other direction, and it will operate into the Sabbath. That the Yesha Council runs it is reported by i24NEWS only and is unconfirmed.

items.headline: Court orders the second Samaria security man held by the Shin Bet moved to house arrest
items.summary: On 15 October, Magistrate's Court Judge Dan Baumann rejected the prosecution's request to extend by eight days the detention of the Samaria security coordinator held by the Shin Bet, and ordered him released to house arrest for seven days. The prosecution said it would ask to delay the order so it can appeal, so his release had not yet taken place when the reports were published. His lawyer, Adv. Nati Rom of Honenu, said he was held in harsh solitary conditions. Samaria council head Yossi Dagan welcomed the decision. Reported by Channel 14, Arutz 7 and Hadashot 04.

items.headline: New herding outpost reported in Wadi Yasuf, east of Salfit
items.summary: WAFA and Sada News reported that on 15 October Israelis set up tents for a new herding outpost in the Wadi Yasuf area, east of Salfit and west of the village of Yasuf. Local Palestinian officials said it would limit residents' access to their land. Only Palestinian outlets have reported it; the exact location and whether the outpost is still in place are unconfirmed.

items.headline: PA commission counts 219 incidents by Israelis in the first 12 days of October
items.summary: The PA's Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission said, in a count WAFA called preliminary, that it recorded 219 incidents by Israeli civilians from 1 to 12 October, 136 of them tied to the olive harvest: 92 attacks on pickers or denial of access to land, and 45 cases of stolen crops or damaged trees. These are PA figures and have not been checked against Israeli data. For comparison, Ynet reported on 13 October that Israeli security officials counted more than 950 Jewish nationalist incidents so far in 2026.
items.section_name: Palestinian Authority Forces and the Threat

items.headline: Settlers begin earthworks at the former Sanur army camp, evacuated in 2005
items.summary: Palestinian outlets reported that on the morning of 15 October a group of Israelis with a bulldozer began leveling land inside the former Sanur military camp south of Jenin, beside the road between Jaba' and Sanur. Israel evacuated the camp in the 2005 disengagement. The report comes from WAFA and was repeated by Al-Ayyam's Raya and other Palestinian outlets. No Israeli source or official response has been found, so the details are unconfirmed by Israeli sources.

items.headline: Catch-up: three more new communities in four weeks, Gad Natan in Gush Etzion, Bitron and Godar in the Jordan Valley
items.summary: Neot Harim is the latest in a run of new communities founded under this year's cabinet decisions. Gad Natan: on Tuesday, Sept. 29, during Sukkot, the community was inaugurated in southern Gush Etzion, between Karmei Tzur and Hebron. It is one of six new communities approved for the Gush Etzion council, and council head Yaron Rosenthal called it the southernmost community in the bloc and the closest to Hebron. Settlement Minister Orit Strock and Heritage Minister Amichai Eliyahu attended (Kipa). The number of families was not reported and is unconfirmed. Bitron: i24NEWS reported on Oct. 4 that 18 of the 20 families in the founding group had already moved onto this new moshav near Route 90 in the Jordan Valley, overlooking the border fence with Jordan. They live in temporary homes while infrastructure work continues. The exact date of the move-in is unconfirmed; one family told i24NEWS it had arrived about a week before. Godar: on Wednesday, Oct. 14, a founding ceremony was held at the foot of Mount Godar in the northern Jordan Valley, between Maskiot and Rotem, on the site once known as Hammam al-Malih. Ministers Nir Barkat, Orit Strock and Amichai Chikli attended. About 12 caravans stand at the site today, and the council plans for about 400 families (Kipa). The number of families now living there was not reported and is unconfirmed. What came before: Ynet reported that in March the Security Cabinet secretly approved 34 new communities in Judea and Samaria, including seven in the Jordan Valley and six in Gush Etzion (not confirmed by a second source).

items.headline: JSR: three rifles seized in Laqef; two suspects arrested
items.summary: JSR reported that police detectives and soldiers of the Ephraim Brigade raided the Arab village of Laqef in Samaria on intelligence about weapons, found three hunting rifles hidden in the village, and arrested two residents in their thirties and sixties for questioning. The account is JSR's, with video credited to the Israel Police spokesperson; a second independent written confirmation was not found for this morning edition.

items.headline: Chief of Staff: the potential for escalation has risen; Division 98 brought into Judea and Samaria
items.summary: Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir held a situation assessment and operational review at Central Command on 14 October and approved plans for continued operations in Judea and Samaria. He said that because of the many warnings in all arenas the potential for escalation has risen, that forces in all sectors have been reinforced and readiness raised, and that Division 98 has been brought into the area to strengthen security; the army is preparing for an attempt to surprise it. Present were Central Command chief Maj. Gen. Avi Bluth, the commanders of the Judea and Samaria Division (Brig. Gen. Kobi Heller), Division 98 (Brig. Gen. Meni Liberty) and Division 96 (Brig. Gen. Oren Simcha), and Shin Bet and Border Police commanders; the same report appeared in Kipa and Olam Katan.

items.headline: Ariel: a vehicle fleeing a checkpoint hits a guard; suspects arrested
items.summary: IDF forces and Judea and Samaria District police operated near Ariel on 14 October after a vehicle whose driver did not obey a guard at a guard post struck him and fled; the guard fired at the vehicle. Security forces arrested several suspects and continued searches and roadblocks. Channel 14 reported that the vehicle had been seen circling Ariel Square several times over two days and was seen entering Salfit, and said at first that no injuries were known; the guard's condition was not published.

items.headline: Six attacks on Israelis in Samaria and Binyamin in one day
items.summary: The Judea and Samaria war room (JSR) listed six incidents on 14 October, four in Samaria and two in Binyamin, all without injuries. They included stones thrown by about 15 olive pickers at an Israeli car on the quarry road south of Deir Abu Mash'al (a window was damaged), stones at a car on Route 60 about 200 meters south of the Givat Assaf junction, stones thrown by dozens of Arabs north of Magen Yehuda and at three residents near Emmanuel, and two Arabs who attacked a shepherd with clubs south of Khirbet a-Tawil. The list also counted the suspected ramming near the Salfit junction; apart from that event, these details have not been confirmed by a second source.

items.headline: Attempt to set fire to Givat Gefen Ami, next to Karmei Tzur
items.summary: Elisha Yered reported on 14 October that Arabs from the village of Beit Ummar tried to set fire to Givat Gefen Ami, a hilltop community next to Karmei Tzur in Gush Etzion, and then fled. Residents put the fire out before it reached nearby trees. Arutz 7 reported a similar arson at the same hill from Beit Ummar in August 2025; no arrests have been reported this time.

items.headline: IDF and Shin Bet raid Addameer in Ramallah and a Hamas charity in Yatta; five arrested
items.summary: The IDF and the Shin Bet said they raided the Ramallah offices of Addameer, which Israel declared a terrorist organization in 2021, on Tuesday 13 October, and in recent weeks the offices of the Islamic Society for Orphan Care in Yatta, which they described as an economic and organizational arm of Hamas. Five activists of Hamas and the Popular Front were arrested, and computers, documents and checkbooks bearing marks of declared Hamas funds were seized. According to the statement, some of the terrorists employed by Addameer took part in the August 2019 bombing at Ein Bubin (Dani's Spring) in which Rina Shnerb was murdered.
items.section_name: Palestinian Authority Forces and the Threat

items.headline: Foreign activist who supports Addameer is arrested near Mitzpe Yair and sent for deportation
items.summary: Judea and Samaria District police arrested a foreign activist on the night of 13 October after a friction incident some days earlier near Mitzpe Yair in the south Hebron hills. Police said she is a founder of the student group MAC, came to intern at Addameer, and had been photographed abroad in a shirt showing Prime Minister Netanyahu with a sniper's crosshairs on his head; she was sent to a Population Authority hearing before deportation. District commander Maj. Gen. Moshe Pinchi said that since the start of 2026, 160 foreign activists have been refused entry and more than 60 deported.

items.headline: IDF destroys the "martyrs" monument in the Jalazone camp near Beit El
items.summary: IDF forces destroyed the "martyrs" monument in the Jalazone refugee camp in the Ramallah district on 14 October; video of the demolition was published by Palestinian outlets. Elisha Yered posted a picture of children from the camp, which lies next to Beit El, standing on the ruins of the monument. The demolition follows the orders signed this month to remove monuments that glorify terrorists.

items.headline: One of the two Samaria security men held by the Shin Bet is released to house arrest
items.summary: One of the two Samaria security men arrested by the Shin Bet at the start of the week was released to house arrest on 13 October, his lawyer, Adv. Asaf Gonen of Honenu, confirmed. On 14 October the wife of the second detainee, whose name is under a gag order, wrote to Shin Bet chief David Zini asking that he be moved from the Shin Bet facility to a regular detention facility. Adv. Nati Rom of Honenu said the detainee is held in a cell of two meters by two meters without daylight.

items.headline: Council heads of Judea and Samaria call for official communities in Areas A and B
items.summary: In a video campaign led by the HaBayta Forum before the elections, Yesha Council chairman and Binyamin council head Israel Ganz, Samaria council head Yossi Dagan, Gush Etzion council head Yaron Rosenthal, Hebron Hills council head Eliram Azulai and Kedumim council head Uziel Vatik called on the government to establish communities and roads in the open land of Areas A and B. Rosenthal cited the government decision that transferred authority in the agreed nature reserve in eastern Gush Etzion from the Palestinian Authority to Israel. Elisha Yered wrote that close to thirty settlement points have been set up in Areas A and B in the last three years; that figure has not been confirmed by a second source.

items.headline: Palestinian report: new outposts since 2023 control about 1.07 million dunams
items.summary: A joint statement by the Palestinian Central Bureau of Statistics and the Environment Quality Authority, issued on 14 October, said that 185 new outposts were set up in Judea and Samaria between 2023 and 2025, about 130 of them shepherding outposts and hilltop sites, holding about 1.07 million dunams, or about 18 percent of the area; about 300,000 dunams were added in 2025 alone. It counted 231 shepherding outposts among about 400 outposts, about 790,000 Israelis living in 170 communities and 400 outposts at the end of July 2026, and Israeli control of 42 percent of the area, 71 percent of Area C and about 91 percent of the Jordan Valley. It also said that 118 Palestinian herding communities left their areas between 2023 and 2025; these are Palestinian Authority figures and have not been checked against Israeli data.
items.source: PLO National Bureau for Defending the Land (citing PCBS)

items.headline: Planning council agenda: 168 homes at Mitzpe Shalem and 275 at Givat Zeev
items.summary: Peace Now's list of plans brought to the Higher Planning Council shows two plans on the agenda for 14 October: final approval (validation) of plan 607/8 for 168 housing units at Mitzpe Shalem, and deposit of plan 215/2/47 for 275 housing units at Givat Zeev. Peace Now counts 10,982 housing units advanced in 2026 including these plans. The result of the meeting has not yet been published.

items.headline: HaShomer HaChadash: a yeshiva north of Jericho within three weeks, and a Haredi city beside it
items.summary: Yoel Zilberman, founder and director of HaShomer HaChadash, told the Ynet and Yedioth Ahronoth conference on 13 October that within three weeks a first yeshiva will be set up at a point called Mahane Sadeh, north of Jericho, next to which a new Haredi city named Ir HaTmarim is to be built. He said the organization set up the first new moshav in Israel in twenty years a month ago, and aims at 150 new communities along the borders. Behadrei Haredim reported that the planned city received a community code from the Interior Ministry in February 2026; that detail has not been checked further.

items.headline: Northern Samaria: Islamic Jihad cell planning an attack is arrested
items.summary: Maariv reported on the morning of 13 October that IDF forces of the Manashe Brigade, directed by the Shin Bet, completed two arrests during the week in the villages of Qabatiya and Arraba, in which four operatives of Islamic Jihad who were planning an attack in northern Samaria were detained. In a separate operation in the Beit Rima area of the Binyamin Brigade, fighters of the Duvdevan unit arrested a wanted man suspected of trafficking in weapons. Channel 14, citing the IDF Spokesperson, reported that the detainees were transferred for further interrogation and that there were no casualties among Israeli forces.

items.headline: Samaria security coordinators block Tapuah Junction over the Shin Bet arrests
items.summary: Hakol Hayehudi reported on 13 October that military security coordinators from Samaria communities blocked Tapuah Junction with their security vehicles in protest at the detention of two Samaria security men arrested by the Shin Bet at the start of the week, under a gag order and initially barred from meeting their lawyers. The slogan of the protest was "A ravshatz is not a terrorist." Adv. Nati Rom of Honenu, who met the detainees after the court accepted the appeal against the meeting ban, said they were being held in harsh conditions in a Shin Bet facility, in a small crowded cell without sunlight and with their eyes covered.

items.headline: Katz answers the High Court: the IDF will remain in the Jenin, Tulkarm and Nur Shams camps
